constitution.title: Indian Constitution
constitution.content:
Sources: UK (Parliamentary system, Rule of Law), USA (Fundamental Rights, Judicial Review), Ireland (DPSP), Canada (Federalism), Australia (Concurrent List), USSR (Fundamental Duties), Germany (Emergency provisions), South Africa (Amendment process), Japan (Procedure Established by Law)

Key Articles:
• Article 1 — Name & territory of Union
• Article 14 — Equality before law
• Article 19 — Six freedoms
• Article 21 — Right to life & personal liberty
• Article 32 — Right to Constitutional Remedies (Heart of Constitution)
• Article 44 — Uniform Civil Code (DPSP)
• Article 51A — Fundamental Duties
• Article 72 — President's pardoning power
• Article 352 — National Emergency
• Article 356 — President's Rule (State Emergency)
• Article 360 — Financial Emergency

Parts (25): Part I — Union & Territory | Part III — Fundamental Rights (Art 12-35) | Part IV — DPSP (Art 36-51) | Part IVA — Fundamental Duties (Art 51A) | Part V — Union Executive | Part VI — State Executive | Part IX — Panchayats | Part IXA — Municipalities

Schedules (12): 1st — States & UTs | 2nd — Salaries of President, Governors, etc. | 3rd — Oaths & Affirmations | 4th — Rajya Sabha seat allocation | 5th — Scheduled Areas & Tribes | 6th — Tribal Areas (Assam, Meghalaya, etc.) | 7th — Union, State, Concurrent Lists | 8th — Official Languages (22) | 9th — Land Reforms (added by 1st Amendment) | 10th — Anti-Defection | 11th — Panchayat powers (73rd Amendment) | 12th — Municipal powers (74th Amendment)

Important Amendments:
• 1st (1951) — Added 9th Schedule for land reforms
• 7th (1956) — Reorganisation of states on linguistic basis
• 42nd (1976) — Added Fundamental Duties & Preamble amendments (Socialist, Secular, Integrity)
• 44th (1978) — Removed Right to Property from FR, made it legal right
• 52nd (1985) — Anti-Defection law
• 61st (1989) — Voting age reduced from 21 to 18
• 73rd (1992) — Panchayati Raj
• 74th (1992) — Urban Local Bodies
• 86th (2002) — Elementary education as fundamental right (Art 21A)
• 101st (2016) — GST
• 103rd (2019) — 10% reservation for EWS
• 106th (2023) — Women reservation in Lok Sabha & Assemblies (33%)

Misc:
• Constituent Assembly formed: Dec 9, 1946 | President: Dr Rajendra Prasad | Chairman of Drafting Committee: Dr B R Ambedkar
• Constitution adopted: Nov 26, 1949 | Enforced: Jan 26, 1950
• Preamble keywords: Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic, Justice, Liberty, Equality, Fraternity
• Basic Structure Doctrine: Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) — Parliament cannot amend basic features
• Types of Writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, Quo Warranto

Landmark Supreme Court Cases:
• Kesavananda Bharati (1973) — Basic Structure Doctrine
• Maneka Gandhi (1978) — Art 21 expanded, procedure must be fair, just, reasonable
• Minerva Mills (1980) — Parliament cannot destroy basic structure, limited amendment power
• SR Bommai (1994) — Art 356 (President's Rule) subject to judicial review
• Indra Sawhney (1992) — 50% cap on reservations, creamy layer concept
• Vishaka (1997) — Guidelines against sexual harassment at workplace
• IR Coelho (2007) — 9th Schedule laws open to basic structure review
• NJAC (2015) — Strikes down NJAC Act, restores collegium system
• Aadhaar (2018) — Upheld as constitutional, but limited private sector use
• Sabarimala (2018) — Ban on women entry unconstitutional
• Section 377 (2018) — Decriminalised homosexuality
• Ayodhya (2019) — Land title to Ram Mandir trust, alternate land for mosque
• Article 370 (2023) — Supreme Court upheld abrogation of Art 370

Constitutional Bodies:
• Election Commission (Art 324) — Superintends elections
• UPSC (Art 315-323) — Central recruiting agency
• Finance Commission (Art 280) — Revenue distribution between Centre & states
• CAG (Art 148) — Audits govt accounts
• Attorney General (Art 76) — Govt's top law officer
• Advocate General (Art 165) — State's top law officer
• National Commission for SCs (Art 338)
• National Commission for STs (Art 338A)
• Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (Art 350B)
• Comptroller & Auditor General (Art 148)

Fundamental Rights (Art 12-35) Details:
• Right to Equality (Art 14-18): 14=equality before law, 15=non-discrimination, 16=equal opportunity in employment, 17=abolition of untouchability, 18=abolition of titles
• Right to Freedom (Art 19-22): 19=6 freedoms (speech, assembly, association, movement, residence, profession), 20=protection against conviction, 21=right to life (expanded via Maneka Gandhi), 21A=right to education, 22=protection against arrest
• Right against Exploitation (Art 23-24): 23=trafficking & forced labour banned, 24=child labour banned (<14 in factories)
• Right to Freedom of Religion (Art 25-28): 25=freedom of conscience, 26=manage religious affairs, 27=no religion tax, 28=no religious instruction in state-funded schools
• Cultural & Educational Rights (Art 29-30): 29=protect minorities' language/script/culture, 30=minorities can establish educational institutions
• Right to Constitutional Remedies (Art 32): SC can issue writs, called "Heart & Soul of Constitution" by Dr Ambedkar

Directive Principles (DPSP) Classification (Art 36-51):
• Socialist principles: 38=welfare state, 39=adequate livelihood, 39A=free legal aid, 41=right to work/education, 42=humane working conditions, 43=living wage, 43A=worker participation in mgmt
• Gandhian principles: 40=gram panchayats, 43=promote cottage industries, 46=SC/ST/OBC uplift, 47=prohibit intoxicants, 48=prohibit cow slaughter
• Liberal-Intellectual: 44=UCC, 45=child care, 48A=protect environment, 49=protect monuments, 50=separate judiciary from executive, 51=international peace
• Minerva Mills case: FR + DPSP balance is basic structure

Union Executive in Detail:
• President: Art 52-62, elected by electoral college, term 5 years, impeachment Art 61, pardoning power Art 72, ordinance power Art 123
• Vice President: Art 63-67, ex-officio Rajya Sabha chair, term 5 years, acts as President when vacancy
• Prime Minister: Art 74-75, appointed by President, council of ministers aids and advises President
• Council of Ministers: 3 categories - Cabinet Ministers (decision makers), Ministers of State (independent or attached), Deputy Ministers
• Cabinet: inner body of CoM, 40-60 members, collective responsibility Art 75(3), individual responsibility Art 75(2)
• Attorney General: Art 76, top law officer, appointed by President, right to speak in Parliament

Parliament in Detail:
• Lok Sabha: Art 81, 543 elected + 2 Anglo-Indian nominated (ended by 104th Amendment), term 5 years, Speaker + Deputy Speaker
• Rajya Sabha: Art 80, 245 members (233 elected by states + 12 nominated), permanent house, 1/3 retire every 2 years, Chairman = VP, Deputy Chairman
• Sessions: 3 per year (Budget, Monsoon, Winter), Quorum = 1/10 of members
• Types of Bills: Ordinary Bill (either house, simple majority), Money Bill (Art 110, Lok Sabha only), Financial Bill, Constitutional Amendment Bill (Art 368, special majority + ratification)
• Parliamentary Committees: Standing (permanent) + Ad hoc (temporary), Financial Committees (PAC, Estimates, Public Undertakings)

Judiciary in Detail:
• Supreme Court: Art 124-147, 1 CJI + 33 judges (34 total), retirement at 65, appointment via Collegium (CJI + 4 senior judges)
• Original Jurisdiction: Art 131 (centre-state disputes, state-state disputes)
• Appellate Jurisdiction: Art 132-136 (constitutional, civil, criminal, special leave petition)
• Advisory Jurisdiction: Art 143 (President can seek SC opinion)
• Writ Jurisdiction: Art 32 (SC), Art 226 (HC)
• High Courts: Art 214-231, 25 HCs, judge retirement at 62, HC can issue writs for FR + ordinary legal rights
• Subordinate Courts: District Courts, Sessions Courts, Magistrate Courts

Centre-State Relations:
• Legislative: Union List (100 items, originally 97), State List (61 items, originally 66), Concurrent List (52 items, originally 47) — 7th Schedule
• Residuary powers: Union (Art 248)
• Administrative: Art 256-263, state must comply with union laws, centre can give directions
• Financial: Art 264-291, taxes divided between Union & State, Finance Commission every 5 years, GST (101st Amendment)
• Provisions for states: Art 356 (President's Rule), Art 360 (Financial Emergency), Governor appointed by President

Emergency Provisions Details:
• National Emergency (Art 352): on war/external aggression/armed rebellion, imposed 3 times (1962 China, 1971 Pak, 1975 internal), 44th Amendment added "armed rebellion" instead of "internal disturbance", must be approved by Parliament within 1 month, can be extended 6 months, Lok Sabha can revoke by simple resolution, FRs suspended except Art 20-21
• President's Rule (Art 356): state emergency, max 3 years (with parliamentary approval every 6 months), 44th Amendment added safeguards, SR Bommai case (1994) made it reviewable
• Financial Emergency (Art 360): never imposed, President can reduce salaries of judges/officials, state money bills reserved for President

Amendment Procedure (Art 368):
• Simple majority: many provisions (new states, creation/abolition of legislative councils, etc.)
• Special majority (2/3 of present + absolute majority): most amendments
• Special majority + ratification by at least half the states: federal provisions (election of President, executive power of Union, SC/HC jurisdiction, distribution of legislative powers, 7th Schedule, representation in Parliament, Art 368 itself)
• Total amendments: 106 (as of 2026)

Important Constitutional Doctrines & Terms:
• Basic Structure Doctrine (Kesavananda Bharati 1973): Parliament cannot alter basic features (supremacy of Constitution, rule of law, judicial review, secularism, democracy, FR, etc.)
• Harmonious Construction: interpret provisions harmoniously
• Pith & Substance: law classified by its true nature
• Colorable Legislation: doing indirectly what can't be done directly
• Doctrine of Severability: invalid part can be separated while keeping valid part
• Doctrine of Eclipse: pre-constitutional laws inconsistent with FR become dormant
• Prospective Overruling: SC can limit its judgement to future cases
• Pleasure Doctrine: President/Governor holds office during pleasure of higher authority
• Pouvoir Constituant vs Pouvoir Législant: constituent power vs legislative power

Key Constitutional Terms:
• Censure Motion vs No-Confidence Motion (both in Lok Sabha only)
• Adjournment vs Prorogation vs Dissolution
• Vote on Account, Supplementary Grant, Excess Grant
• Cut Motion (Policy Cut, Economy Cut, Token Cut)
• Calling Attention Motion, Short Duration Discussion
• Privilege Motion, Breach of Privilege, Contempt of the House
• Lame Duck Session (last session before Lok Sabha dissolution)
• Guillotine (closure of debate on demands for grants)
• Quorum, Whip, Defection (10th Schedule)
• Point of Order, Walking Out, Boycott
• President's Address (Art 87): first session after each election + first session each year
• Questions: Starred (oral answer), Unstarred (written), Short Notice, Questions to Private Members

schemes.title: Government Schemes
schemes.content:
Major Central Schemes (with launch year & ministry):

• Ayushman Bharat-PMJAY (2018, Health) — World's largest health insurance, ₹5 lakh/family/yr, 10 cr+ families
• PM-KISAN (2019, Agriculture) — ₹6,000/yr to farmers in 3 installments
• PM Awas Yojana (Urban) (2015, Housing) — Housing for all by 2022 (extended)
• PM Awas Yojana (Gramin) (renamed from IAY) — Rural housing
• Jal Jeevan Mission (2019, Jal Shakti) — Tap water connection to every rural household by 2024
• Swachh Bharat Mission (2014, Drinking Water & Sanitation) — Open Defecation Free (ODF) India
• Ujjwala Yojana (2016, Petroleum) — Free LPG connections to BPL families
• PM Jan Dhan Yojana (2014, Finance) — Financial inclusion, zero-balance accounts
• Make in India (2014, Commerce) — Boost manufacturing, 25 sectors
• Digital India (2015, Electronics & IT) — Digital infrastructure, e-governance
• Skill India (2015, Skill Dev) — Training 40 cr people by 2022
• Startup India (2016, Commerce) — Tax holidays, funding, easier compliance
• Stand-Up India (2016) — Bank loans to SC/ST/women entrepreneurs
• Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (2015, Women & Child) — Improve child sex ratio
• POSHAN Abhiyaan (2018, Women & Child) — Reduce malnutrition/stunting
• PM Mudra Yojana (2015, Finance) — Loans up to ₹10L for micro enterprises (Shishu, Kishor, Tarun)
• PM Fasal Bima Yojana (2016, Agriculture) — Crop insurance at low premium
• PM Kisan Maan Dhan Yojana (2019) — Pension ₹3,000/month for small farmers after 60
• Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY) — Health insurance for BPL
• Sansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (2014) — MPs adopt villages for model development
• PM Poshan Shakti Nirman (Mid-Day Meal) — Hot cooked meals in govt schools
• One Nation One Ration Card (2019) — Nationwide portability of food security
• National Education Policy 2020 — 5+3+3+4 system, multiple entry/exit
• AMRUT (2015, Housing & Urban) — Basic infrastructure in 500 cities
• Smart Cities Mission (2015) — 100 smart cities
• SAGARMALA (2015, Shipping) — Port-led development
• Bharatmala Pariyojana (2017, Road Transport) — Highway development (~65,000 km)
• PM Gati Shakti (2021) — National Master Plan for connectivity
• National Hydrogen Mission (2021) — Green hydrogen production
• Pradhan Mantri Vishwakarma (2023) — Support for traditional artisans & craftspeople
• PM-JAY (Ayushman Bharat) expanded — Free health cover to all 70+ citizens
• PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (2024) — Solar power for 1 crore households
• PM Schools for Rising India (PM SHRI) (2022) — Upgrade 14,500+ schools
• Missions under NEP 2020: NIPUN Bharat (foundational literacy), DIKSHA, SWAYAM, Academic Bank of Credit
• PM e-Bus Sewa (2022) — 10,000 e-buses for city transport
• PM Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN) (2023) — Tribal welfare
• Aspirational Districts Programme (2018) — Development of 112 backward districts
• Aspirational Blocks Programme (2022) — Block-level development
• SVAMITVA (2020) — Property card via drone survey for rural areas
• PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) — Working capital for street vendors
• National Migrant Information System (NMIS) — Tracking of migrant workers
Scheme Budget & Coverage Details:
• PM-KISAN: ₹60,000+ cr annual budget, 11+ cr farmers
• Ayushman Bharat: ₹6,400 cr (2023-24), 24 cr+ beneficiaries, 25,000+ empaneled hospitals
• PM Awas Yojana: 3.5+ cr houses approved, ₹80,000+ cr budget
• Jal Jeevan Mission: ₹3.6L cr outlay, 12+ cr tap connections provided (75%+ rural coverage)
• Swachh Bharat: 11+ cr toilets built, 6L+ ODF villages
• Ujjwala: 10+ cr connections, ₹1,600 subsidy per cylinder
• PM Jan Dhan: 50+ cr accounts opened, ₹2L+ cr deposits
• MUDRA: 40+ cr loans sanctioned, ₹20L+ cr disbursed

Flagship Social Welfare Schemes:
• National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP): pension for elderly/widows/disabled
• PM Matru Vandana Yojana: ₹5,000 maternity benefit for first child
• PM Suraksha Bima Yojana: accidental insurance ₹2L/yr, premium ₹12/yr
• PM Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana: life insurance ₹2L, premium ₹330/yr
• Atal Pension Yojana: guaranteed pension ₹1,000-5,000/month
• PM Kisan Maan Dhan Yojana: ₹3,000/month pension after 60 for small farmers
• Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana: ₹30,000 health cover for BPL

Agriculture & Rural Development:
• PM Fasal Bima Yojana: lowest premium in world (1.5-5%), 3.5+ cr farmers covered
• PM Krishi Sinchai Yojana: "Per Drop More Crop", micro-irrigation focus
• PM Kisan Sampada Yojana: food processing infrastructure
• e-NAM: electronic agri-trading platform, 1,000+ mandis integrated
• PM Formalization of Micro Food Processing Enterprises
• National Mission on Natural Farming: promote chemical-free farming
• Soil Health Card Scheme: 25+ cr cards issued
• MGNREGA: 100 days guaranteed wage employment, ₹89,000+ cr budget

Education & Skill Development:
• NEP 2020: 5+3+3+4 system, multiple entry/exit, vocational from class 6
• PM SHRI Schools: 14,500+ schools upgraded as model schools
• NIPUN Bharat: foundational literacy & numeracy by 2026-27
• DIKSHA: digital teacher training platform (1 crore+ teachers)
• SWAYAM: free online courses from class 9 to PG
• SWAYAM Prabha: 32 DTH education channels
• PM e-Vidya: multi-mode access to education
• National Digital Education Architecture (NDEAR)
• Skill India: 1+ cr youth trained, 38 Sector Skill Councils
• PM Kaushal Vikas Yojana: skill training with certification
• National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS)

Infrastructure & Connectivity:
• Bharatmala: 65,000 km highways, ₹10.6L cr outlay
• SAGARMALA: port modernization, ₹1L cr+ investment
• UDAN (Regional Connectivity): affordable flights, 500+ routes
• PM Gati Shakti: multi-modal connectivity, NMP platform
• National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP): ₹111L cr, 9,000+ projects
• Dedicated Freight Corridors: Eastern (1,856 km) + Western (1,506 km)
• Sagarmala: port-led development, 7+ new ports
• Bharatmala Phase 2: 7,000 km expressways
• Setu Bharatam: bridges & flyovers for accident-free highways

Digital & Financial Inclusion:
• Digital India: 5L+ Common Service Centres, UMANG app, DigiLocker, Aadhaar
• BHIM-UPI: world's leading real-time payment system, 500+ cr transactions/month
• Account Aggregator framework: data sharing consent-based
• ONDC: open e-commerce network
• National Digital Health Mission: 50+ cr health IDs created
• National Data Governance Framework
• PM Gati Shakti - National Master Plan for multi-modal connectivity
• National Geospatial Policy 2022

Recent Schemes (2023-25):
• PM Vishwakarma Yojana: ₹15,000 cr for 18 traditional trades
• PM Surya Ghar: free electricity via rooftop solar for 1 cr households
• PM-JANMAN: ₹24,000 cr for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)
• National Common Mobility Card (One Nation One Card)
• Mission Mausam: weather & climate resilience (2024)
• National Quantum Mission: quantum computing (2023)
• PM e-Bus Sewa: 10,000 e-buses, ₹57,000 cr
• Green Hydrogen Mission: ₹19,744 cr, 5 MMT target by 2030
• BioE3 Policy: biotech for economy, environment, employment
• PM Awas Yojana 2.0: additional 2 cr houses

sports.title: Sports
sports.content:
Major Tournaments & Trophies:
• Cricket — World Cup (ODI/T20), Champions Trophy, Ashes (Eng-Aus), Ranji Trophy (domestic), Irani Cup, Duleep Trophy, Vijay Hazare Trophy
• Football — FIFA World Cup, Asian Cup, Durand Cup (India's oldest), Santosh Trophy, I-League, ISL
• Hockey — Hockey World Cup, Sultan Azlan Shah Cup, Champions Trophy, Asia Cup
• Tennis — Grand Slams: Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon, US Open; Davis Cup, Fed Cup
• Badminton — Thomas Cup (men's team), Uber Cup (women's team), Sudirman Cup (mixed), BWF World Championships
• Olympics — Modern Olympics started 1896 (Athens); IOC HQ: Lausanne; Motto: Citius-Altius-Fortius
• Asian Games — Started 1951 (New Delhi); OCA HQ: Kuwait
• Commonwealth Games — Started 1930; CGF HQ: London
• Khelo India — National programme for grassroots sports development

Major Sports Awards:
• Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna (earlier Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna) — Highest sports award
• Arjuna Award — Consistent performance over 4 years
• Dronacharya Award — Excellence in coaching
• Dhyan Chand Award — Lifetime achievement
• Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Trophy — Best overall university

National Sports Days:
• National Sports Day — August 29 (Dhyan Chand's birthday)
• National Youth Day — January 12 (Swami Vivekananda's birthday)
• International Yoga Day — June 21

Important Venues:
• Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad — World's largest (1.32L capacity)
• Eden Gardens, Kolkata — Largest cricket stadium originally
• Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai
• MA Chidambaram Stadium, Chennai
• Major Dhyan Chand Stadium, New Delhi (hockey)
• SAI centres across India

Sports Terms: Deuce (tennis), Love (tennis), LBW (cricket), Stalemate (chess), Checkmate (chess), Hat-trick, Grand Slam, Century, Golden Duck, Silly Point (cricket), Birdie/Bogie (golf), KO (boxing), Volley (football/tennis), Dribble (football/basketball), Clean sweep

India's Olympic Medals (by sport):
• Hockey: 8 gold, 1 silver, 4 bronze (most successful)
• Shooting: 1 gold (Abhinav Bindra, 2008), 5 silver, 5 bronze
• Wrestling: 7 medals (Sushil Kumar, Bajrang Punia, Ravi Dahiya, Sakshi Malik, etc.)
• Badminton: 3 medals (Saina Nehwal, PV Sindhu, etc.)
• Boxing: 3 medals (Vijender Singh, MC Mary Kom, Lovlina Borgohain)
• Athletics: Neeraj Chopra — gold (javelin, 2020), silver (2024)
• Weightlifting: 2 medals (Karnam Malleswari, Mirabai Chanu)
• Tennis: 1 medal (Leander Paes)

Major Indian Sporting Firsts:
• First Olympic gold (individual): Abhinav Bindra (2008, 10m air rifle)
• First Olympic medal: Norman Pritchard (1900, athletics, 2 silver)
• First cricket World Cup win: 1983 (Kapil Dev)
• First T20 World Cup win: 2007 (MS Dhoni)
• First Chess Grandmaster: Viswanathan Anand (1988)
• First Indian woman to win an Olympic medal: Karnam Malleswari (2000)
• First Asian Games host: New Delhi 1951

Chess in India:
• Viswanathan Anand — 5-time World Champion (2000, 2007, 2008, 2010, 2012)
• D Gukesh — Youngest undisputed world champion (2024, age 18)

• Humpy Koneru, Harika Dronavalli — top women GMs
• India won Chess Olympiad gold 2024 (both men's & women's teams)

books.title: Books & Authors
books.content:
Famous Indian Writers & Their Works:
• Rabindranath Tagore — Gitanjali (Nobel 1913), Ghare-Baire, The Home and the World
• Mahatma Gandhi — The Story of My Experiments with Truth (autobiography), Hind Swaraj
• Jawaharlal Nehru — The Discovery of India, An Autobiography, Glimpses of World History
• Dr B R Ambedkar — Annihilation of Caste, The Buddha and His Dhamma, Pakistan or Partition
• RK Narayan — Malgudi Days, Swami and Friends, The Guide (Sahitya Akademi Award)
• Amartya Sen — The Argumentative Indian, Development as Freedom, Poverty and Famines
• APJ Abdul Kalam — Wings of Fire (autobiography), Ignited Minds, India 2020
• Shashi Tharoor — The Great Indian Novel, An Era of Darkness, Inglorious Empire
• Arundhati Roy — The God of Small Things (Booker Prize 1997)
• Salman Rushdie — Midnight's Children (Booker Prize 1981, Booker of Bookers), The Satanic Verses
• Vikram Seth — A Suitable Boy (one of longest novels in English), The Golden Gate
• VS Naipaul — A House for Mr Biswas, India: A Wounded Civilization (Nobel 2001)
• Amish Tripathi — The Immortals of Meluha (Shiva Trilogy), Ram Chandra Series
• Chetan Bhagat — Five Point Someone, One Night @ the Call Center, The 3 Mistakes of My Life
• Arvind Adiga — The White Tiger (Booker Prize 2008)
• Jhumpa Lahiri — Interpreter of Maladies (Pulitzer), The Namesake
• Kiran Desai — The Inheritance of Loss (Booker Prize 2006)
• Amitav Ghosh — The Shadow Lines, The Glass Palace, Ibis Trilogy
• Ramachandra Guha — India After Gandhi, Gandhi: The Years That Changed the World
• Ruskin Bond — The Blue Umbrella, Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra

Sahitya Akademi Award: India's highest literary honour, established 1954

Important Ancient Texts:
• Vedas: Rig (oldest), Yajur, Sama, Atharva
• Upavedas: Ayurveda, Dhanurveda, Gandharvaveda, Sthapatyaveda
• Upanishads: 108, main 13 (Ish, Kena, Katha, Prashna, Mundaka, etc.)
• Epics: Ramayana (Valmiki), Mahabharata (Ved Vyasa)
• Puranas: 18 Mahapuranas, 18 Upapuranas
• Arthashastra — Chanakya/Kautilya
• Ashtadhyayi — Panini (Sanskrit grammar)
• Rajatarangini — Kalhana (Kashmir history)

Other Notable Writers & Works:
• Mulk Raj Anand — Coolie, Untouchable (social realism)
• Raja Rao — Kanthapura, The Serpent and the Rope
• Khushwant Singh — Train to Pakistan, A History of the Sikhs
• Mahasweta Devi — Hajar Churashir Maa, Breast Stories (tribal rights)
• Vijaydan Detha — Rajasthani folk tales (Padma Shri 2023)
• Namita Gokhale — Paro: Dreams of Passion, Things to Leave Behind
• Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni — The Palace of Illusions (Mahabharata from Draupadi's view)
• Anita Desai — Clear Light of Day, Fasting, Feasting
• William Dalrymple — The Last Mughal, White Mughals (British historian on India)
• Dominique Lapierre — The City of Joy (Kolkata)

Indian Literature Awards (recent):
• Jnanpith 2023: Damodar Mauzo (Konkani), 2024: Gulzar (Urdu)
• Sahitya Akademi 2023: Neelam Sachdeva (English, The Lost Country)
• International Booker 2023: Geetanjali Shree (Tomb of Sand — Hindi)

Key Literary Terms:
• Autobiography — self-written life story
• Biography — life story written by another

space.title: ISRO & Space
space.content:
ISRO — Indian Space Research Organisation
• Founded: 1969 | HQ: Bengaluru | Chairman: S Somanath (as of 2026)
• Vision: Harness space tech for national development
• Department of Space (DOS) under PMO

Key Milestones:
• 1963: First sounding rocket (Nike-Apache) from Thumba, Kerala
• 1975: First Indian satellite — Aryabhata (launched by USSR)
• 1979: First experimental flight — SLV-3 (partial success)
• 1980: SLV-3 success — India became 6th country in space
• 1983: INSAT-1B — First multipurpose communication satellite
• 1993: PSLV maiden flight (partial failure)
• 1994: PSLV-G fully successful
• 2001: GSLV maiden flight
• 2008: Chandrayaan-1 — Discovered water molecules on Moon
• 2013: Mangalyaan (MOM) — India first Asian country to reach Mars, 4th in world
• 2017: PSLV-C37 — Launched 104 satellites in single mission (world record)
• 2019: Chandrayaan-2 — Orbiter successful, lander Vikram crashed
• 2023: Chandrayaan-3 — First country to soft-land near Moon's south pole!
• 2023: Aditya-L1 — India's first solar mission
• 2024: Gaganyaan test flights — India's first human spaceflight program

Launch Vehicles:
• SLV-3 — India's first (retired)
• ASLV — Augmented (retired)
• PSLV — Workhorse, 50+ flights, most reliable
• GSLV — Geosynchronous, cryogenic upper stage
• GSLV Mk III / LVM3 — Heavy lift, can carry 4T to GTO
• SSLV — Small satellite launcher (new)
• NGLV — Next Generation (under development)

Satellite Series:
• INSAT — Communication (geostationary)
• IRS — Remote sensing
• CARTOSAT — Earth observation
• NAVIC (IRNSS) — India's own GPS (7 satellites)
• GSAT — Communication satellites
• RISAT — Radar imaging
• Oceansat — Oceanography

Space Centres:
• VSSC — Thumba (launch vehicles)
• SDSC-SHAR — Sriharikota (launch site)
• URSC — Bengaluru (satellites)
• SAC — Ahmedabad (payloads)
• LPSC — Valiamala (propulsion)
• IIST — Trivandrum (space education)
• NE-SAC — Shillong (North East applications)
• ISTRAC — Bengaluru (tracking)

Other Space Agencies: NASA (USA, 1958), Roscosmos (Russia), ESA (Europe), CNSA (China), JAXA (Japan)

Recent & Upcoming (2025-26):
• Gaganyaan — First unmanned test flight (TV-D1) completed Oct 2023, manned H1 2025
• NISAR — NASA-ISRO Earth observation satellite, 2025
• SPADEX — Space docking experiment (Dec 2024)
• Chandrayaan-4 — Lunar sample return (planned)
• Venus Orbiter (Shukrayaan) — Planned after 2025
• Bharatiya Antariksha Station — India's space station by 2035
• Indian Moon landing by 2040
• XPoSat — X-ray polarimetry (Jan 2024)
• INSAT-3DS — Weather satellite (Feb 2024)
• Startups: Skyroot, Agnikul, Pixxel, Digantara — private space revolutionISRO Launch Vehicles Technical Details: — SLV-3: 17m, 2-stage solid, 40kg to LEO (1980). ASLV: 24m, 5-stage, 150kg to LEO (2 failures). PSLV: 44m, 4-stage (solid+liquid), 3,800kg to LEO/1,800kg to SSO, 50+ flights, Core Alone (PSLV-CA), XL variant (PSLV-XL with larger boosters), usually 6 strap-on boosters. GSLV: 49m, 3-stage, 2,500kg to GTO, indigenous cryogenic upper stage (CE-7.5). LVM3 (GSLV MkIII): 43.5m, 3-stage, 4,000kg to GTO, 8,000kg to LEO, S200 solid boosters (largest solid motors), L110 liquid core, C25 cryogenic upper stage (CE-20). SSLV: 34m, 3-stage solid, 500kg to LEO, on-demand launch, 4 failures. NGLV: reusable, under development, 10,000kg to GTO target

All ISRO Chairman History: — Vikram Sarabhai (1963-71, founder), M G K Menon (1972), Satish Dhawan (1972-84, transformed ISRO), U R Rao (1984-94), K Kasturirangan (1994-2003), G Madhavan Nair (2003-09), K Radhakrishnan (2009-14), A S Kiran Kumar (2015-18), K Sivan (2018-22), S Somanath (2022-)

All Chandrayaan Missions Detailed: — Chandrayaan-1 (2008): first Indian Moon mission, PSLV-XL, discovered water on Moon (M3 instrument), orbiter lasted 312 days. Chandrayaan-2 (2019): LVM3, orbiter+linder (Vikram)+rover (Pragyan), orbiter still functioning, lander crashed due to braking thrust error. Chandrayaan-3 (2023): LVM3, lander (Vikram)+rover (Pragyan), first country to soft-land near south pole, rover confirmed presence of sulphur, mission lasted 1 lunar day (14 Earth days)

All Mangalyaan/Mars Missions: — Mars Orbiter Mission (2013-2022): PSLV-XL, India first Asian country to Mars, 4th in world, mission lasted 8 years (designed for 6 months), five payloads (MCC, TIS, MSM, MENCA, LAP). Mangalyaan-2/Mars Orbiter Mission 2: planned, will include lander

Gaganyaan & Human Spaceflight: — India's first human spaceflight program, 3 astronauts (Group Captain Prashanth Nair, Angad Pratap, Ajit Krishnan), IAF test pilots, trained in Russia, TV-D1 test flight (Oct 2023) — crew module abort & parachute test, planned orbital flight H1 2025, Vyommitra (female robot astronaut), ISRO Human Space Flight Centre (HSFC, Bengaluru)

Other Indian Space Missions & Satellites: — AstroSat (2015): India's first multi-wavelength space observatory. XPoSat (2024): X-ray polarimetry. Aditya-L1 (2023): first solar mission, placed at Lagrange point L1, 7 payloads, studying solar corona. NAVIC/IRNSS: 7 satellites, India's own GPS, standard position service 20m accuracy. GSAT series: 30+ communication satellites. RISAT series: radar imaging satellites (all-weather). CARTOSAT series: high-resolution earth observation. Oceansat: ocean & atmospheric studies. INSAT: oldest series, weather & communication. ResourceSat: land & water resources.

International Space Collaboration: — NISAR (NASA-ISRO): L&S band SAR satellite, 2025. TRISHNA (ISRO-CNES): thermal infrared. AstroSat collaboration (Canada, UK, USA). LUPEX (ISRO-JAXA): lunar polar exploration. ISS collaboration: Indian experiments. UN affiliated: UN-CESM (Centre for Space Education in Asia-Pacific). IN-SPACe: single-window for private sector participation. NewSpace India Limited (NSIL): commercial arm.

Private Space Sector in India: — IN-SPACe (2020) promoting private sector, NewSpace India Ltd (NSIL, 2019). Startups: Skyroot Aerospace (Vikram rocket launch 2022), Agnikul Cosmos (3D-printed engine), Pixxel (hyperspectral satellites), SatSure (satellite analytics), Digantara (space debris tracking), Bellatrix Aerospace (electric propulsion), Dhruva Space (satellite platforms), GalaxEye (SAR imaging), Abyom Space Tech, TakeMe2Space.

dance.title: Dance Forms
dance.content:
Classical Dances of India (8 Sangeet Natak Akademi recognized):

1. Bharatanatyam — Tamil Nadu. Features: fixed upper torso, bent legs, intricate footwork, expressive gestures (mudras). Pioneers: Rukmini Devi Arundale
2. Kathak — Uttar Pradesh. Features: fast spins (chakkars), rhythmic footwork, storytelling. Lucknow, Jaipur, Raigarh gharanas. Birju Maharaj
3. Kathakali — Kerala. Features: Elaborate makeup (green/red/black), eye movements, storytelling from epics. Costume-heavy
4. Kuchipudi — Andhra Pradesh. Features: Singing + dancing, fast rhythms, copper pot balance. Gone with the Wind
5. Odissi — Odisha. Features: Tribhangi (three-bend posture), fluid upper body, independent footwork. Gotipua tradition
6. Manipuri — Manipur. Features: Graceful, soft movements, no heavy ankle bells, circular patterns. Rasleela themes
7. Mohiniyattam — Kerala. Features: Feminine (Mohini=celestial enchantress), gentle swaying, white & gold costume
8. Sattriya — Assam. Features: Monastic origin, fast rhythmic patterns, from Vaishnavite monasteries (Sattras)

Also recognized as classical: Chhau (Odisha/Jharkhand/WB — mask dance)

• Jammu & Kashmir: Rouf, Hafiza, Dumhal, Hikat
• Himachal: Nati, Kullu, Kinnauri

Kathak (Mughal influence, chakkars/turns, tatkar footwork, thaat/amad/toda/paran compositions, Bindadin Maharaj gharana founder). Kathakali (Kerala, pachcha/green noble, kathi/knife villain, thadi/red beard, kari/black, minukku/female; mudras 24 basic). Kuchipudi (originally male dancers, singing+dancing, brass plate dance, Tarangam footwork). Odissi (tribhangi three bends, chauka square stance, sculptural poses from temple carvings, gotipua tradition by young boys dressed as females). orgs.title: International Organizations
orgs.content:
United Nations (UN): Founded 1945 | HQ: New York | Members: 193
• UN Charter signed June 26, 1945 (San Francisco) | Effective Oct 24, 1945 (UN Day)
• Principal Organs: General Assembly (all members), Security Council (15 — 5P+10E), ECOSOC (54), ICJ (15 judges, The Hague), Secretariat (SG), Trusteeship Council (inactive)
• Security Council P5: USA, UK, France, Russia, China (veto powers)
• UN Secretaries-General: Guterres (Portugal, current), Ban Ki-Moon, Kofi Annan, Boutros-Ghali, Perez de Cuellar, Waldheim, Thant, U Thant (only Asian), Hammarskjöld
• India at UN: Founding member, supports expansion of SC, G4 member (India, Brazil, Germany, Japan)

UN Agencies & Reports:
• WHO (1948, Geneva) — World Health Report, World Health Statistics
• UNESCO (1945, Paris) — Education for All, World Heritage Sites
• UNDP (1965, NY) — Human Development Index (HDI), Human Development Report
• UNEP (1972, Nairobi) — Emissions Gap Report, Global Environment Outlook
• UNFCCC (1992, Bonn) — Climate change framework, COP conferences
• IMF (1944, Washington DC) — World Economic Outlook, Article IV consultations
• World Bank (1944, Washington DC) — World Development Report, Ease of Doing Business
• WTO (1995, Geneva) — World Trade Report, Trade Policy Review
• ILO (1919, Geneva) — World Employment and Social Outlook, International Labour Standards
• FAO (1945, Rome) — State of Food Security and Nutrition, Food Price Index
• IAEA (1957, Vienna) — Atoms for Peace, nuclear safeguards
• UNICEF (1946, NY) — State of the World's Children
• UNHCR (1950, Geneva) — Global Trends Report, refugees
• WFP (1961, Rome) — Food aid, hunger eradication
• UNODC (1997, Vienna) — World Drug Report, Crime
• ITU (1865, Geneva) — Global Connectivity Report
• UPU (1874, Bern) — Postal development

Other Key Organizations:
• NATO (1949, Brussels) — 32 members, military alliance
• European Union (1951/93, Brussels) — 27 members
• BRICS (2009) — Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, +5 new (2024: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi, UAE)

• SCO (2001, Beijing) — Security & economic cooperation (8 members)
• G7 — Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, UK, USA + EU

• OPEC+ — OPEC + 10 allies including Russia

• AIBA/OCA/IPC — Sports bodies
• IAEA — Atomic energy

• ICJ — UN judicial organ
• ICC (2002, The Hague) — War crimes, genocide
• WHO — Health

India's Role in Key Organizations:
• UN: Founding member, G4 member (for SC expansion)
• BRICS: Founding member, hosts BRICS CCI
• SCO: Full member (2017)
• SAARC: Founding member
• G20: Member, hosted 2023 summit in New Delhi

• AIIB: Founding member, HQ Beijing

• FATF: Member since 2010 (combat money laundering)
• MTCR: Member since 2016 (missile technology control)
• Wassenaar Arrangement: Member (2017)
• Australia Group: Member (2018)UN Security Council Details:
• 15 members (5P+10E). P5: USA, UK, France, Russia, China (veto power).
• 10 non-permanent elected for 2 years by GA (5 from Africa+Asia, 2 from Latin America, 2 from Western Europe, 1 from Eastern Europe).
• India elected 8 times (most recent 2021-22).
• Reform proposals: G4 (India, Brazil, Germany, Japan) demand permanent seats.
• Uniting for Consensus (Italy, Korea, Pakistan, etc.) oppose.
• Veto usage: USSR/Russia 143, USA 86, UK 30, France 16, China 20 (as of 2026)

UN Reports & Indices (India Rankings):
• HDI 2024: India 134th, 0.644
• GHI 2024: India 105th, 27.3 serious
• World Happiness Report: India 126th
• Global Peace Index: India 116th
• Corruption Perception Index: India 93rd, 40/100
• Ease of Doing Business: India 63rd (2020, discontinued)
• Global Gender Gap Index: India 129th
• Press Freedom Index: India 161st
• Climate Change Performance Index: India 7th among largest emitters
• Global Innovation Index: India 40th

World Trade Organization (WTO):
• Established 1995 (replaced GATT 1948). HQ Geneva. 166 members.
• Ministerial Conference (highest body, meets every 2 years).
• Singapore issues: investment, competition, transparency in procurement, trade facilitation.
• Doha Development Round (2001, stalled). Bali Package 2013 (trade facilitation).
• India's key issues: food security subsidies, agriculture market access, services (Mode 4), special safeguard mechanism, patent flexibilities.
• TRIPS, TRIMS, GATS agreements. Dispute Settlement Body (DSB).
• MC13 Abu Dhabi 2024.

International Financial Institutions:
• IMF (1944, 190 members, HQ DC, MD Kristalina Georgieva).
• World Bank Group: IBRD (middle-income), IDA (poorest), IFC (private), MIGA (guarantees), ICSID (disputes).
• ADB (1966, Manila, 68 members, India 4th largest shareholder).
• AIIB (2016, Beijing, 100+ members, China largest shareholder).
• NDB (BRICS, Shanghai, 2014).
• FATF (1989, Paris, 40 recommendations, grey list). India member since 2010.

Regional Organizations & India's Role:
• SAARC (1985, 8 members, Kathmandu, India largest).
• BIMSTEC (1997, 7 members, Bay of Bengal).
• ASEAN (1967, 10 members, India is Summit Partner).
• Quad (India, USA, Japan, Australia). SCO (2001, 9 members).
• NAM (Non-Aligned Movement, 1961, 120 members).
• G4 (India, Germany, Japan, Brazil — UNSC reform).
• BASIC (India, China, Brazil, S Africa — climate).

Disarmament & Nuclear Treaties:
• NPT (1968, 190 parties, India not signatory).
• CTBT (1996, India not signatory). FMCT (under negotiation).
• MTCR (India joined 2016). Wassenaar Arrangement (2017). Australia Group (2018).
• NSG (India applied, not yet member). India de facto nuclear weapon state (2005 civil nuclear deal).

Environmental & Climate Agreements:
• UNFCCC (1992, Rio). Kyoto Protocol (1997). Paris Agreement (2015, NDCs).
• India's NDC: reduce emissions intensity 45% by 2030 (from 2005), 500 GW non-fossil, net zero by 2070.
• Montreal Protocol (1987, ozone, Kigali Amendment for HFCs).
• Convention on Biological Diversity (1992). Nagoya Protocol. UNCCD. Stockholm Convention. Basel Convention. CITES.
• LiFE movement (Lifestyle for Environment) proposed by India.

• States with most dams: Maharashtra (>1,000), MP, Gujarat, Karnataka
• Large dams in India: ~5,700 (3rd in world after USA, China)
• Dam Safety Act 2021.
