history.title: Indian History
history.content:
Ancient India (Pre-history to 1206 AD):
Indus Valley Civilization (3300-1300 BC): Major sites: Harappa (Punjab, Pak), Mohenjo-Daro (Sindh), Dholavira (Gujarat), Rakhigarhi (Haryana), Lothal (Gujarat - dockyard). Also Kalibangan (Rajasthan - ploughed field), Banawali (Haryana), Surkotada (Gujarat - horse evidence). Town planning: grid system, burnt bricks, drainage, Great Bath (Mohenjo-Daro). Crop: wheat, barley, cotton (first to grow cotton). Animals: cattle, buffalo, sheep, goat, pig, elephant, rhinoceros, camel; no horse except Surkotada. Seals: Pashupati seal (proto-Shiva), unicorn motif. Script: pictographic, undeciphered. Religion: Mother Goddess, fertility cult, tree worship. Decline: flood, climate change, Aryan migration theories.
Vedic Period (1500-600 BC): Rig Veda (oldest, 1028 hymns, 10 mandalas, Gayatri mantra), Samaveda (melodies), Yajurveda (prose rituals), Atharvaveda (magic spells). Brahmanas (ritual commentaries), Aranyakas (forest texts), Upanishads (philosophy, 108 total, Mukhya 13). Key concepts: Brahman (universal soul), Atman (individual soul), Karma, Samsara (rebirth), Moksha (liberation). Early Vedic: tribal society, pastoral, no caste rigidity, women attended sabha/samiti. Later Vedic: varna system, janapadas, rice cultivation, iron use. Kingdoms: Kuru, Panchala, Kosala, Videha. Mahajanapadas (16): Magadha (strongest, capital Rajgriha then Pataliputra), Kosala, Avanti, Vatsa, etc.
Mahajanapadas & Religious Movements (600-322 BC): Buddhism (Gautam Buddha, 563 BC, Lumbini Nepal, 4 sights, Mahabodhi Temple Bodh Gaya, First Sermon Sarnath, died Kushinagar), 4 Noble Truths, 8-fold Path, Sangha, Tripitaka (Vinaya, Sutta, Abhidhamma). Jainism (Mahavira, 540 BC, Kundagrama, 5 vows: ahimsa, satya, asteya, brahmacharya, aparigraha), Triratna (right faith, right knowledge, right conduct), Digambara/Svetambara sects. Magadha dynasties: Haryanka (Bimbisara-Ajatashatru), Shishunaga, Nanda (Mahapadma Nanda).
Mauryan Empire (322-185 BC): Chandragupta (322-298 BC), defeat of Nandas, Chanakya (Kautilya, Arthashastra). Bindusara (298-272 BC). Ashoka (268-232 BC), Kalinga War (261 BC), Dhamma policy, Rock Edicts, Pillar Edicts, Lion Capital (Sarnath), stupas (Sanchi). Administration: 5 divisions, Patliputra capital, Kautilya's Saptanga theory. Decline after 185 BC, Pushyamitra Shunga coup.
Post-Mauryan & Sangam Age (185 BC-300 AD): Shungas (Pushyamitra), Kanvas, Satavahanas (Gautamiputra Satakarni). Indo-Greeks (Menander/Milinda), Sakas (Rudradaman), Kushans (Kanishka, Gandhara art, Mathura school, 4th Buddhist Council). Sangam literature in Tamil (Tolkappiyam, Silappadikaram, Manimekalai), Pandya, Chera, Chola kingdoms.
Gupta Empire (300-550 AD - Golden Age): Chandragupta I (319-335), Samudragupta (335-375, Allahabad Prashasti by Harisena), Chandragupta II (375-415, Vikramaditya, Fahien visit, Ujjain capital). Kumaragupta (Nalanda University). Skandagupta (Huna repulsion). Harsha (606-647, Kannauj, Hieun Tsang, Nalanda, Priyadarshika). Science: Aryabhata (mathematics, astronomy), Varahamihira (Brihat Samhita), Sushruta (surgery), Charaka (medicine). Literature: Kalidasa (Abhijnanasakuntalam), Vishakhadatta (Mudrarakshasa), Panchatantra.
Early Medieval & Regional Kingdoms (550-1206 AD): Vardhana (Harsha), Pushyabhuti dynasty. Chalukyas (Pulakeshin II, Badami, Aihole), Pallavas (Mahendravarman, Narasimhavarman, Mamallapuram, Kanchi), Rashtrakutas (Amoghavarsha, Ellora Kailasa temple). Palas (Dharmapala, Nalanda). Pratiharas (Gurjara-Pratihara). Cholas (Rajaraja I, Rajendra I, Brihadeeswara Temple, Tanjore, naval expansion to Srivijaya). Rajputs: Paramara (Bhoja, Dhar), Chauhan (Prithviraj III, Tarain 1192), Solanki (Kumarapala), Gahadavala (Jaichandra).
Delhi Sultanate (1206-1526): Slave/Mamluk (Qutbuddin Aibak, Iltutmish, Balban, Razia Sultana). Khalji (Alauddin Khalji, Malik Kafur, market control, Mongol repulsion). Tughlaq (Muhammad bin Tughlaq - token currency, Daulatabad shift, taxation in Doab; Firoz Shah Tughlaq). Sayyid (Khizr Khan). Lodi (Bahlul, Sikandar, Ibrahim - Panipat 1526). Architecture: Qutb Minar, Alai Darwaza, Alauddin's Siri fort, Tughlaqabad, Firoz Shah Kotla.
Vijayanagara & Bahmani Kingdoms (1336-1646): Vijayanagara: Harihara & Bukka (Sangama dynasty), Krishnadevaraya (Tuluva, 1509-1529, Amuktamalyada, Portuguese trade, Battle of Talikota 1565). Hampi (UNESCO). Bahmani: Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah, Mahmud Gawan. Deccan Sultanates: Ahmadnagar, Berar, Bijapur, Golconda, Bidar.
Mughal Empire (1526-1857): Babur (Panipat 1526, Khanwa 1527, Chanderi 1528, Ghaghra 1529). Humayun (Suri interlude - Sher Shah Suri, Grand Trunk Road, Rupee, Dak chowki). Akbar (1556-1605, Bairam Khan, Panipat II 1556, Rajput policy, Din-i-Ilahi, Navratnas (Tansen, Birbal, Todar Mal, etc.), Fatehpur Sikri, Buland Darwaza, Ibadat Khana, Mansabdari system, Zabt system, Sulh-i-Kul). Jahangir (1605-1627, Nur Jahan, Sir Thomas Roe/Metcalf). Shah Jahan (1627-1658, Taj Mahal, Red Fort, Peacock Throne, Shahjahanabad, Mumtaz Mahal). Aurangzeb (1658-1707, Deccan campaigns, Maratha conflict, Sikh rebellion, Jizya, Zakat, Fatwa-e-Alamgiri). Later Mughals: Bahadur Shah I, decline after Nadir Shah's 1739 invasion. Architecture: Humayun's Tomb, Taj Mahal (Ustad Ahmad Lahauri, 22 yrs, 20K workers, complete 1653), Red Fort, Jama Masjid, Agra Fort, Lahore Fort, Shalimar Gardens.
Maratha Empire (1674-1818): Shivaji (1630-1680, Coronation Raigad 1674, Ashta Pradhan, guerilla warfare, forts (Raigad, Sinhagad, Pratapgad), Treaty of Purandar). Peshwas: Balaji Vishwanath, Baji Rao I (expansion to north, Malwa, Bundelkhand), Balaji Baji Rao (Third Battle of Panipat 1761). Maratha confederacy (Scindia, Holkar, Gaikwad, Bhonsle). Anglo-Maratha Wars: 1st (1775-82, Treaty of Salbai), 2nd (1803-05), 3rd (1817-18, Peshwa Baji Rao II defeated).
European Arrival & Expansion (1498-1757): Vasco da Gama (Calicut 1498), Portuguese (Goa 1510, Albuquerque), Dutch (Pulicat, Surat), English (1619, Surat, Madras 1639, Bombay 1668, Calcutta 1690), French (Pondicherry 1673, Dupleix). Carnatic Wars: 1st (1746-48), 2nd (1749-54), 3rd (1756-63). Battle of Plassey (1757, Clive vs Siraj-ud-Daulah, Mir Jafar betrayed). Battle of Buxar (1764, Munro vs Shuja-ud-Daulah, Shah Alam II, Mir Qasim). Dual system of Clive in Bengal (1765-72). Regulating Act 1773, Warren Hastings (Governor-General 1773-85, 1st Anglo-Maratha, 2nd Mysore, Reforms).
Company Aftermath & British Raj (1765-1857): Cornwallis (Permanent Settlement 1793, Bengal, Zamindari, police reforms). Wellesley (Subsidiary Alliance, 4th Mysore 1799, 2nd Anglo-Maratha). Dalhousie (Doctrine of Lapse: Satara, Jhansi, Nagpur, Awadh; railways, telegraph, postal). Social reforms: Sati abolition (1829, Bentinck, Raja Ram Mohan Roy), Widow Remarriage Act 1856 (Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar). Revolt of 1857: Mangal Pandey (Barrackpore), Rani Lakshmibai, Tantia Tope, Bahadur Shah Zafar (Delhi). Causes: greased cartridges, Doctrine of Lapse, heavy taxes, resentment. Suppressed by 1858.
Modern Indian Nationalism (1885-1947): Indian National Congress (1885, A.O. Hume, W.C. Bonnerjee first president). Moderates: Dadabhai Naoroji (drain theory), Gokhale, Ranade. Extremists: Tilak (Swaraj is my birthright), Lala Lajpat Rai, Bipin Chandra Pal (Lal-Bal-Pal trio), Aurobindo Ghosh. Partition of Bengal (1905, Curzon), Swadeshi & Boycott movement. Muslim League (1906, Dhaka). Minto-Morley Reforms 1909. Surat split 1907. Home Rule Movement (1916, Tilak-Annie Besant). Lucknow Pact 1916. Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms 1919 (dyarchy). Rowlatt Act 1919, Jallianwala Bagh (Apr 13, 1919, General Dyer). Gandhian phase: Champaran Satyagraha (1917 - indigo), Kheda (1918), Ahmedabad mill strike (1918). Non-Cooperation (1920-22, Chauri Chaura 1922). Simon Commission 1928 (Lala Lajpat Rai death). Nehru Report 1928. Lahore session 1929 (Purna Swaraj). Dandi March (Mar 12-Apr 6, 1930). Civil Disobedience (1930-31). Gandhi-Irwin Pact 1931. Round Table Conferences (1930-32). Communal Award 1932 (MacDonald). Poona Pact 1932. Government of India Act 1935 (provincial autonomy). Quit India Movement (1942, Do or Die, August Kranti). INA (Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose). Royal Indian Navy Mutiny 1946. Cabinet Mission 1946 (rejected by Muslim League). Direct Action Day Aug 16, 1946. Mountbatten Plan Jun 3, 1947. Indian Independence Act Jul 18, 1947. Partition & Independence Aug 15, 1947.
Indian National Movement Leaders: Mahatma Gandhi (1869-1948, 4 mass movements, 21-day fast for untouchability, Harijan). Jawaharlal Nehru (1889-1964, PM 1947-64, socialist, non-alignment). Sardar Patel (1875-1950, integration of 565 princely states, Iron Man). Subhas Chandra Bose (1897-1945, INA, Azad Hind Govt, Singapore). Bhagat Singh (1907-31, Lahore conspiracy, Simon Commission protest). Rajendra Prasad (1884-1963, President of Constituent Assembly). Maulana Azad (1888-1958, first education minister). B.R. Ambedkar (1891-1956, Constitution chairman, Dalit rights). Vallabhbhai Patel (Barrister, Bardoli Satyagraha 1928).
Important Battles in Indian History:
• 1st Battle of Tarain (1191): Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Ghori
• 2nd Battle of Tarain (1192): Ghori defeated Prithviraj, Delhi Sultanate begins
• 1st Battle of Panipat (1526): Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi, Mughal Empire begins
• Battle of Khanwa (1527): Babur defeated Rana Sanga
• Battle of Chanderi (1528): Babur defeated Medini Rai
• Battle of Ghaghra (1529): Babur defeated Afghans
• 2nd Battle of Panipat (1556): Akbar (Bairam Khan) defeated Hemu
• Battle of Haldighati (1576): Akbar vs Maharana Pratap (Mughal won, Pratap escaped)
• Battle of Plassey (1757): Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah (British Bengal)
• Battle of Buxar (1764): Munro defeated combined Mughal-Bengal-Awadh forces
• 3rd Battle of Panipat (1761): Ahmad Shah Abdali defeated Marathas
• Battle of Wandiwash (1760): British defeated French (Carnatic)
• Anglo-Mysore Wars (1767-1799): British defeat Tipu Sultan at Srirangapatnam (1799)
• Anglo-Sikh Wars (1845-46, 1848-49): British annex Punjab
• Battle of Talikota (1565): Deccan Sultanates defeated Vijayanagara

geography.title: Indian Geography
geography.content:
Physical Geography of India:
Location & Extent: Area 3.287M sq km (7th largest). Lat 8°4'N-37°6'N, Long 68°7'E-97°25'E. Tropic of Cancer (23°30'N) passes through 8 states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, WB, Tripura, Mizoram. SI unit: Standard Meridian 82°30'E (Mirzapur, UP) - IST (UTC+5:30). Southernmost point - Indira Point (Andaman & Nicobar), drifted during 2004 tsunami. Northernmost - Indira Col (Siachen). Total land border ~15,200 km. Coastline ~7,516 km (including islands).
Physiographic Divisions: 1) Northern Mountains (Himalayas: 3 parallel ranges - Himadri/Greater Himalayas avg 6000m, Himachal/Lesser Himalayas 2000-3000m, Shivaliks/Outer 900-1200m). 2) Northern Plains (Indus-Ganga-Brahmaputra basin, ~2400 km, bhabar/terai/bhangar/khaddar). 3) Peninsular Plateau (Central Highlands - Malwa Plateau, Bundelkhand, Baghelkhand, Chotanagpur; Deccan Plateau - Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana). 4) Indian Desert (Thar, Rajasthan). 5) Coastal Plains (Western - Konkan, Kanara, Malabar; Eastern - Coromandel, Northern Circars). 6) Islands (Andaman & Nicobar - 572 isles, 3 groups: North/Middle/Andaman & Nicobar; Lakshadweep - 36 isles, 11 inhabited, Minicoy).
Himalayan Ranges: Karakoram (Siachen, K2/Godwin Austen 8611m), Zaskar (Nanga Parbat 8126m, Kargil), Ladakh (Indus valley), Pir Panjal (Jawahar Tunnel, Rohtang Pass), Dhauladhar (Himachal). Great Himalayas (Mt Everest 8848m, Kanchenjunga 8586m, Makalu 8481m, Dhaulagiri 8167m) - all ranges have glacial passes. Important Passes: Zoji La (Kargil), Niti Pass (Uttarakhand), Shipki La (HP), Nathu La (Sikkim), Bomdi La (Arunachal), Khardung La (Ladakh, world's highest motorable at 5359m).
River Systems: Himalayan rivers: Indus (3,180 km, 5 tributaries - Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej), Ganga (2,525 km, origin Gangotri, Bhagirathi + Alaknanda at Devprayag, major tributaries - Yamuna, Ghaghra, Gandak, Kosi, Son), Brahmaputra (2,900 km, origin Tibet, enters at Namcha Barwa, world's largest river island Majuli). Peninsular rivers: Narmada (west-flowing, rift valley, 1,312 km), Tapi (west-flowing, 724 km). East-flowing: Godavari (1,465 km, longest peninsular, Paithan/Jayakwadi dam), Krishna (1,400 km, Nagarjuna Sagar, Almatti), Kaveri (805 km, Mettur, Krishnarajasagar), Mahanadi (851 km, Hirakud dam).
Climate & Seasons: Tropical monsoon. 4 seasons: Winter (Dec-Feb), Summer/Mar-May (hot, Loo in north), SW Monsoon Jun-Sep (Bay of Bengal branch - Kolkata to Delhi; Arabian Sea branch - Mumbai, Kerala first state, Mawsynram highest rainfall 11871mm), Retreating NE Monsoon Oct-Nov (Tamil Nadu coast). Western Disturbances (winter rain in NW India). El Nino (drought risk), La Nina (good monsoon).
Soil Types: Alluvial (43%, northern plains - khaddar/bhangar, wheat/rice/sugarcane), Black/Regur (16%, Deccan trap - cotton), Red & Yellow (18%, Tamil Nadu/Karnataka/Chhattisgarh - millets), Laterite (8%, Western Ghats/North East - tea/coffee), Arid/Desert (4%, Rajasthan), Saline (coastal), Peaty (Kerala - kari soils), Forest (Himalayas).
Natural Vegetation: Tropical Rainforest (Western Ghats, NE, Andaman - ebony, mahogany), Tropical Deciduous (teak, sal, bamboo - most extensive), Thorn Forests (Rajasthan, acacia), Mountain Forests (pine, deodar, fir at increasing altitude), Mangroves (Sundarbans, Bhitarkanika, Pichavaram). Forest cover ~24.56% of area (2023 ISFR).
Agriculture & Crops: Kharif (Jun-Oct: rice, cotton, jute, sugarcane, maize, groundnut, soybean). Rabi (Oct-Mar: wheat, mustard, gram, barley, peas). Zaid (short season between: watermelons, cucumber, fodder). Green Revolution (1960s, Norman Borlaug, M.S. Swaminathan, wheat/rice, Punjab/Haryana/UP). Cropping regions: rice (WB largest, Punjab highest productivity), wheat (UP largest), sugarcane (UP, Maharashtra), cotton (Gujarat), coffee (Karnataka), tea (Assam, WB Darjeeling), jute (WB, Bihar), rubber (Kerala).
Mineral & Energy Resources: Iron ore (Odisha - Keonjhar, Mayurbhanj; Karnataka - Bellary, Chitradurga; Goa). Coal (Jharia, Raniganj, Bokaro, Talcher, Neyveli). Petroleum (Mumbai High, ONGC, Assam - Digboi, Gujarat - Ankleshwar, Rajasthan - Barmer). Natural Gas (Krishna-Godavari Basin, Mumbai High). Nuclear (Uranium - Jaduguda Jharkhand, Tummalapalle AP; Thorium - Kerala monazite sands). Bauxite (Odisha, Gujarat, Jharkhand). Mica (Jharkhand, Bihar, Rajasthan). Copper (Malajkhand MP, Khetri Rajasthan).
Power Sector: Installed capacity ~440 GW (2025). Thermal (coal) ~55%. Hydro ~11%. Nuclear ~2%. Renewable ~32% (Solar ~80 GW, Wind ~45 GW, Biopower ~10 GW, Small Hydro ~5 GW). Largest thermal plants: Vindhyachal MP (4.76 GW). Largest hydro: Tehri (1 GW). Largest solar: Bhadla Rajasthan (2.2 GW). National Solar Mission target 500 GW non-fossil by 2030.
Multipurpose River Projects: Bhakra Nangal (Sutlej, HP/Punjab), Damodar Valley (WB/Jharkhand, flood control + power), Hirakud (Mahanadi, Odisha, world's largest earthen dam), Nagarjuna Sagar (Krishna, Telangana), Sardar Sarovar (Narmada, Gujarat), Tehri (Bhagirathi, Uttarakhand), Tungabhadra (Karnataka/AP), Indira Gandhi Canal (Rajasthan, longest canal in India ~650 km).
Mountain Peaks: K2 (8611m, Karakoram, 2nd highest world), Kanchenjunga (8586m, Sikkim, 3rd highest), Nanda Devi (7816m, Uttarakhand), Kamet (7756m, Uttarakhand), Saltoro Kangri (7742m, Siachen), Anamudi (2695m, Kerala highest), Doddabetta (2636m, Nilgiris), Mahendragiri (1501m, Odisha), Guru Shikhar (1722m, Mt Abu, Rajasthan highest).
Important Lakes: Wular (J&K, largest freshwater), Chilika (Odisha, largest coastal, lagoon), Sambhar (Rajasthan, largest salt lake), Loktak (Manipur, phumdis floating islands), Dal (Srinagar, houseboats), Pulicat (AP/TN border, 2nd largest brackish), Kolleru (AP, freshwater between Krishna & Godavari), Vembanad (Kerala, longest in India, backwaters), Pangong Tso (Ladakh, brackish, 5th largest in Asia), Tso Moriri (Ladakh, Ramsar site).
National Highways: NH 1 (Delhi-Ambala), NH 2 (Delhi-Kolkata, now part of NE1/NE2), NH 44 (Srinagar-Kanyakumari, longest ~3,745 km, North-South corridor), NH 48 (Delhi-Chennai via Jaipur, Ahmedabad, Mumbai). Golden Quadrilateral (Delhi-Mumbai-Chennai-Kolkata ~5,846 km). East-West Corridor (Porbandar-Silchar). North-South Corridor (Srinagar-Kanyakumari). Bharatmala project (65,000 km of highways).
Smart Cities Mission: 100 cities selected (2015). Pune, Ahmedabad, Bhubaneswar top performers. Key features: smart water, waste, energy, mobility, e-governance. AMRUT 2.0: universal water supply to 4,723 ULBs.
Population & Census (2011): Total ~1.21B. Density 382/km2. Sex ratio 940 (females/1000 males). Literacy 74.04%. Decadal growth 17.64%. Most populous state: UP (199M). Least: Sikkim (6L). Most literate: Kerala (94%). Most densely populated: Bihar (1106/km2). Least dense: Arunachal (17/km2). Sex ratio best: Kerala (1084). Worst: Haryana (879).
Natural Disasters in India: Floods (Bihar 2008/Kosi, Uttarakhand 2013/Kedarnath, Kerala 2018/2019, Assam annual). Cyclones (Odisha 1999 super cyclone, Phailin 2013, Hudhud 2014, Amphan 2020, Yaas 2021, Mocha 2023). Earthquakes (Bhuj 2001 7.7, Kashmir 2005 7.6, Sikkim 2011 6.9, Nepal 2015 impact on India). Tsunami (2004 Indian Ocean, 10m waves, affected TN, Andaman, Kerala ~10,700 deaths in India). Landslides (Western Ghats, Himalayas, Konkan region). Droughts (Marathwada, Bundelkhand, Rajasthan).
Climate Change & India: Net zero target by 2070. Panchamrit: 500 GW non-fossil by 2030, 50% energy from renewables, 1B ton CO2 reduction. IPCC reports, National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) 2008: 8 missions (Solar, Water, Energy, Green India, etc.). State Action Plans on Climate Change (SAPCC). Green Credit Programme 2023.
Indian Ocean & Maritime Geography: India's Exclusive Economic Zone ~2.37M sq km. Three seas: Arabian Sea (west), Bay of Bengal (east), Indian Ocean (south). Strategic chokepoints: Strait of Malacca (India to Pacific), Hormuz (energy), Bab-el-Mandeb (Red Sea). SAGAR (Security And Growth for All in the Region) policy. Sagarmala project - port modernization. 13 major ports & 200+ minor ports.

economy.title: Indian Economy
economy.content:
Indian Economy Overview:
Basic Concepts: GDP (Gross Domestic Product - total value of goods/services within India). GNP (GDP + net income from abroad). NDP = GDP - depreciation. NNP = GNP - depreciation (also called National Income). GDP at factor cost vs market price (market price = factor cost + net indirect taxes). GDP nominal vs real (real adjusts for inflation). GDP deflator (Nominal GDP/Real GDP x 100). Growth rate: current ~6-7% (2025), target 8%. Structure: Agriculture ~16%, Industry ~28%, Services ~56%. India 5th largest economy (after US, China, Germany, Japan).
Budgets & Fiscal Policy: Union Budget presented by Finance Minister on Feb 1 (since 2017), earlier was Feb 28/29. Railway Budget merged with General Budget (2017). Fiscal deficit: total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings (target <4.5% of GDP by 2025-26). Revenue deficit: revenue expenditure - revenue receipts. Primary deficit: fiscal deficit - interest payments. FRBM Act (2003): Fiscal Responsibility & Budget Management. Direct taxes (Income Tax, Corporate Tax) vs Indirect taxes (GST, Customs, Excise). Budget estimates vs Revised estimates vs Actuals. Finance Commission (15th FC: 2021-26, Chairman N.K. Singh) determines tax revenue sharing between Centre & states (41% share to states).
Banking & Monetary Policy: RBI (Reserve Bank of India, established 1935, nationalized 1949, Governor Shaktikanta Das until 2025). Functions: monetary policy, currency issue, banker to government, banker to banks, forex management. Monetary Policy Committee (MPC): 6 members (3 RBI + 3 external), meets bi-monthly, sets repo rate. Current instruments: Repo Rate (RBI lends to banks), Reverse Repo (RBI borrows from banks), CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio - % of deposits kept with RBI), SLR (Statutory Liquidity Ratio - % kept in safe assets), MSF (Marginal Standing Facility - emergency), Bank Rate, Open Market Operations (OMO). Inflation targeting: 4% +-2% (flexible inflation targeting). CPI (Consumer Price Index) used as inflation measure. Base rate: minimum lending rate of banks. MCLR (Marginal Cost of Funds based Lending Rate). NPA (Non-Performing Asset - loan overdue >90 days). Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) for weak banks. PSBs (Public Sector Banks): SBI, PNB, Canara, Bank of Baroda, etc. Total PSBs reduced from 27 to 12 through mergers (2019-20).
Insurance & Pension: IRDAI (Insurance Regulatory & Development Authority of India). LIC (Life Insurance Corporation, 1956). Pension: EPFO (Employees' Provident Fund Org), NPS (National Pension System - PFRDA), APY (Atal Pension Yojana).
Financial Markets: SEBI (Securities & Exchange Board of India, established 1988, statutory 1992). Stock Exchanges: BSE (Bombay Stock Exchange, 1875, SENSEX - 30 stocks), NSE (National Stock Exchange, 1992, NIFTY 50 - 50 stocks). Index types: broad (SENSEX/NIFTY), sectoral (NIFTY Bank, NIFTY IT, etc.), market-cap (Large, Mid, Small-Cap). Derivatives: Futures, Options (FO segment). IPOs (Initial Public Offering). FPI (Foreign Portfolio Investor) vs FDI (Foreign Direct Investment). Demat accounts (NSDL/CDSL). NIFTY 50: top 50 traded stocks on NSE, base 1000 (1995). SENSEX: 30 oldest largest stocks, base 100 (1979).
Taxation: GST (Goods & Services Tax, 101st Amendment, Jul 1, 2017). One Nation One Tax. 4 slabs: 5% (essentials), 12%, 18% (majority), 28% (luxury + cess). CGST (Central) + SGST (State) for intra-state; IGST (Integrated) for inter-state. GST Council (chaired by Union FM, all state FMs) decides rates and rules. Latest: GST on online gaming 28% (2023). Compensation Cess to states ended Sep 2024. GST revenue ~₹1.7L-2L cr/month (2025-26). Direct Tax: Income Tax (slabs: 0-3L nil, 3L-7L 5%, 7L-10L 10%, 10L-12L 15%, 12L-15L 20%, >15L 30% as per New Regime - no exemptions). Corporate Tax: 22% for domestic (no exemptions)/15% for new manufacturing. PLI scheme for 14 sectors: mobile, pharma, auto, etc.
Inflation & Prices: Types: Demand-Pull (too much money), Cost-Push (input price rise), Headline (food+fuel+core), Core (excluding food & fuel). WPI (Wholesale Price Index - weekly, base 2011-12). CPI (Consumer Price Index - monthly, base 2012-13). CPI-IW (Industrial Workers) used for DA. CPI-AL (Agricultural Labour). CPI-RL (Rural Labour). Inflation targeting: MPC targets CPI at 4%±2%. WPI base year revised from 2004-05 to 2011-12. CPI base year revised to 2012-13. Urban CPI vs Rural CPI. Food inflation measured by Consumer Food Price Index (CFPI).
External Sector: Balance of Payments (BoP): Current Account (exports-imports of goods/services + remittances + investment income) + Capital Account (FDI, FPI, loans, banking capital). CAD (Current Account Deficit) when imports > exports. Forex Reserves ~$650B (2025, 4th largest globally after China, Japan, Switzerland). Rupee depreciation: managed float. EXIM Policy (Foreign Trade Policy 2023-28: target $2T exports by 2030). Special Economic Zones (SEZ Act 2005). EPCG, MEIS, RoDTEP schemes. Export: engineering goods, petroleum, gems & jewellery, pharma, textiles, chemicals, agriculture. Import: crude oil, gold, electronics, machinery, coal, chemicals.
Agriculture & Food Management: MSP (Minimum Support Price - 22 crops, recommended by CACP). PDS (Public Distribution System - NFSA 2013, 5 kg grain/person/month). Procurement: FCI (Food Corporation of India). PM-KISAN (₹6000/yr). PM-FBY (crop insurance). Kisan Credit Card scheme. Operation Flood (milk revolution, Amul). Operation Green (potato, onion, tomato price stabilisation). National Agriculture Market (e-NAM). Food processing mega parks (PMKSY).
Industry & Infrastructure: Index of Industrial Production (IIP, base 2011-12). Core Industries (8 sectors: coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery, steel, cement, electricity, fertilizers - 40.27% weight in IIP). Ease of Doing Business (India 63rd rank in 2019). Make in India (25 sectors). Industrial corridors: Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor (DMIC), Chennai-Bengaluru, Amritsar-Kolkata. Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme (14 sectors, ₹1.97 lakh cr). Pradhan Mantri Gati Shakti National Master Plan 2021 (multi-modal connectivity). National Logistics Policy 2022.
Poverty & Employment: Poverty Line (Tendulkar 2011: ₹27/day rural, ₹33/day urban; Rangarajan 2014: ₹32 rural, ₹47 urban). NITI Aayog MPI (Multidimensional Poverty Index) - health, education, standard of living. MGNREGA (100 days guaranteed wage employment). PLFS (Periodic Labour Force Survey). Unemployment rate ~7-8% (2025-26). Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR ~40%). Skill India Mission (Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana).
Important Economic Committees: Surjit Bhalla (latest poverty estimates). Arvind Panagariya (15th FC). Raghuram Rajan/Urjit Patel (monetary policy committees/Financial Sector Legislative Reforms). C. Rangarajan (poverty definition). Vijay Kelkar (tax reforms). Y.V. Reddy (PFRDA). Raja Chelliah (tax reforms 1991). Disinvestment: NITI Aayog recommends CPSE for divestment, DIPAM manages. LIC IPO (2022, largest IPO in India).
Major Economic Reforms: 1991 (Narasimham-Mammohan Singh: LPG - Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation; abolished licence raj, reduced tariffs, allowed FDI). GST 2017 (indirect tax unification). Insolvency & Bankruptcy Code (IBC) 2016 (time-bound resolution). Jan Dhan 2014 (financial inclusion). Demonetisation 2016 (₹500/₹1000 banned, 86% currency withdrawn, digital push). Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT, ₹7 lakh+ cr saved). RERA 2016.
Economic Terms: Base Rate, Repo, SLR, CRR, GDP, GVA, NNP, CAD, BoP, Laffer Curve, Phillips Curve, Gini Coefficient, HDI, Lorenz Curve, Quantum Index, Purchasing Power Parity (PPP), Human Capital Index, PLFS, CPI, WPI, IIP, PMI (Purchasing Managers Index), CACP, FCI, ECA (Essential Commodities Act), SBI, SEBI, IRDAI, PFRDA, CCI (Competition Commission), TRAI, NHAI, PPP model, Viability Gap Funding (VGF), Green Bonds, Masala Bonds, ECB (External Commercial Borrowings), ADR/GDR, Dividend, Bonus, Buyback, Corporate Governance, ESG, SDG.
India & World Economy: G20 (India president 2023). BRICS (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, expanded 2024: Iran, Egypt, Ethiopia, UAE, Indonesia). SCO (Shanghai Cooperation Organisation). WTO (India GATT member, Marrakesh 1994). IMF & World Bank (India founding member). ADB (Asian Development Bank). NDB (New Development Bank - BRICS Bank, HQ Shanghai). AIIB (Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, HQ Beijing). FATF (Financial Action Task Force). Quad (India, USA, Japan, Australia - economic cooperation). IPEF (Indo-Pacific Economic Framework). India-EFTA trade deal 2024.

science.title: General Science
science.content:
Physics:
Mechanics: Newton's 3 Laws of Motion (1st-Law of Inertia, 2nd-F=ma, 3rd-Action-Reaction). Speed = distance/time, Velocity v=s/t (vector), Acceleration a=(v-u)/t. Force: F=ma, Weight W=mg, Mass is constant everywhere, Work: W=F×d, Energy: Kinetic (KE=½mv²) & Potential (PE=mgh). Power = Work/Time (Watt). Momentum p=mv, Conservation of momentum. Laws of Thermodynamics: 1st (energy conservation), 2nd (entropy increases), 3rd (absolute zero -273.15°C unattainable). Heat transfer: conduction (solids), convection (fluids), radiation (electromagnetic waves). Pressure: P=F/A (Pascal). Atmospheric pressure 1 atm = 101325 Pa = 760 mm Hg. Boyle's Law (PV=const at constant T), Charles's Law (V∝T at constant P), Archimedes' Principle (buoyant force = displaced fluid weight). Bernoulli's Principle (P + ½ρv² + ρgh = constant).
Sound & Waves: Sound needs medium, speed in air ~343 m/s, water ~1482 m/s, steel ~5960 m/s. Frequency (Hz): audible 20-20,000 Hz, infrasound (<20 Hz - elephants), ultrasound (>20 kHz - bats, sonar). Amplitude→loudness, Frequency→pitch. Doppler Effect (frequency shift when source/observer moves). Echo. SONAR (Sound Navigation & Ranging). Supersonic: >Mach 1 (343 m/s).
Light & Optics: Speed of light 3×10⁸ m/s in vacuum, slows in denser medium. Reflection (angle i=r), Refraction (Snell's Law: n₁sinθ₁=n₂sinθ₂). Lenses: convex (converging, forms real/inverted or virtual/upright, used for hypermetropia), concave (diverging, used for myopia). Power of lens P=1/f (Dioptre). Human eye: cornea→pupil→lens→retina→optic nerve. Defects: Myopia (near-sighted, concave lens), Hypermetropia (far-sighted, convex lens), Presbyopia (bifocals), Astigmatism (cylindrical lens). Rainbow: dispersion of white light into 7 colours (VIBGYOR). Primary colours: Red, Green, Blue (RGB additive). Fibre optics: total internal reflection. Lasers: coherent, monochromatic, high intensity. Applications: barcode scanner, CD/DVD, surgery, LIDAR.
Electricity & Magnetism: Ohm's Law V=IR. Circuit elements: Resistor (R), Capacitor (C), Inductor (L). Power P=VI=I²R=V²/R. AC vs DC: Alternating Current (50 Hz in India) vs Direct Current. Transformers: step-up (increase voltage) or step-down. Electromagnet: current-carrying coil, used in motors, generators, MRI, cranes. Magnetic field patterns: Bar magnet, Earth's magnetic field (North pole near geographic South). Fleming's Left Hand Rule (motor) & Right Hand Rule (generator). Electric motor (AC/DC). Generator (dynamo/alternator). Domestic wiring: Earth wire (safety), Fuse/MCB (short circuit protection), 240V AC, 50 Hz.
Electronics & Modern Physics: Diodes (one-way current), Transistors (amplifier/switch), IC (integrated circuit). Capacitors store charge. Solar cell (photovoltaic effect, p-n junction). LED (light emitting diode, forward bias, less power). CCD (image sensor). Radioactivity: alpha (α - He nucleus), beta (β - electron), gamma (γ - electromagnetic wave). Half-life. Nuclear fission (splitting heavy nucleus - U-235, nuclear reactors) vs Fusion (joining light nuclei - H to He in Sun, tokamak). Radioisotopes: Co-60 (cancer therapy), I-131 (thyroid), C-14 (carbon dating), U-235 (nuclear fuel). Roentgen discovered X-rays (1895), Becquerel (radioactivity 1896), Curie (radium), Rutherford (nucleus), Bohr (atomic model), Chadwick (neutron), Fermi (nuclear reactor).
Chemistry:
Atomic Structure: Atom: nucleus (protons + neutrons) + electrons in shells. Atomic Number Z = number of protons, Mass Number A = Z + N (neutrons). Isotopes: same Z, different N (e.g., C-12, C-13, C-14). Isobars: same A, different Z. Isotones: same N. Ions: cation (+), anion (-). Shells: K(2), L(8), M(18), N(32). Valence electrons determine chemical properties. Periodic Table: 118 elements, 18 groups, 7 periods. Groups: 1 (Alkali metals), 2 (Alkaline earth), 17 (Halogens), 18 (Noble gases). Periods: 1 (2 elements), 2 & 3 (8 each), 4 & 5 (18 each), 6 (32 incl Lanthanides), 7 (32 incl Actinides). Mendeleev (1869, periodic law by atomic mass), Moseley (1913, rearranged by atomic number).
Chemical Bonding & Reactions: Ionic bond (metal+non-metal, electron transfer, e.g., NaCl), Covalent bond (non-metal+non-metal, sharing, e.g., H₂O, CO₂), Metallic bond (metal lattice, delocalized electrons). Valency: number of electrons lost/gained/shared. Oxidation: loss of electrons (gain of oxygen). Reduction: gain of electrons (loss of oxygen). Redox reactions: both occur together. Electrolysis: decomposition by electricity. Electroplating. Acids: sour, pH <7 (HCl, H₂SO₄, HNO₃). Bases: bitter, pH >7 (NaOH, KOH). Salts: neutralization (acid+base→salt+water). pH scale: 0-14, neutral=7. Indicators: litmus (red in acid, blue in base), phenolphthalein (colourless in acid, pink in base).
Metals & Non-Metals: Metals: conductors, malleable, ductile, lustrous (Fe, Cu, Al, Au, Ag, Na, Mg, K, Ca, Zn, Pb, Hg liquid). Non-metals: insulators, brittle (O, N, H, C, S, P, Cl, I). Metalloids: B, Si, Ge, As, Sb, Te. Alloys: Brass (Cu+Zn), Bronze (Cu+Sn), Stainless steel (Fe+Cr+Ni+C), Solder (Pb+Sn), Nichrome (Ni+Cr), Duralumin (Al+Cu+Mg+Mn). Corrosion: rusting of iron (Fe₂O₃·xH₂O), tarnishing of silver (Ag₂S), green patina on copper (CuCO₃·Cu(OH)₂).
Important Chemicals & Compounds: Water (H₂O, universal solvent, density 1 g/cc, bp 100°C). Carbon: diamond (hardest, insulator), graphite (soft, conductor), fullerene (C₆₀). CO₂ (greenhouse gas, dry ice solid CO₂). Ammonia (NH₃, fertilizer). Sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄, king of chemicals). NaOH (caustic soda). NaHCO₃ (baking soda). Na₂CO₃ (washing soda). CaO (quicklime). Ca(OH)₂ (slaked lime, whitewash). CaSO₄·½H₂O (plaster of Paris). CaCO₃ (limestone, marble). H₂O₂ (hydrogen peroxide, bleaching). C₂H₅OH (ethanol, alcohol). CH₃COOH (acetic acid, vinegar). CH₄ (methane, natural gas). C₃H₈ (LPG). C₈H₁₈ (petrol octane). Soap: Na/K salts of fatty acids, micelle formation. Detergent: synthetic surfactant. Explosives: TNT, RDX, Nitroglycerine.
Environmental Chemistry: Ozone layer (O₃ in stratosphere, UV protection, CFC depletion, Montreal Protocol 1987). Global warming: CO₂, CH₄, N₂O, HFCs - Paris Agreement 2015. Pollution: Air (SO₂, NOx, PM2.5/10, AQI), Water (BOD, COD, eutrophication, heavy metals), Soil (pesticides, plastic). Acid rain: SO₂+NOx+H₂O→H₂SO₄+HNO₃. Smog: classical (sulphur + soot) vs photochemical (NOx + VOCs + sunlight → ozone).
Biology:
Cell Biology: Cell: basic unit of life. Prokaryotic (no nucleus - bacteria) vs Eukaryotic (nucleus - plants, animals). Organelles: Nucleus (DNA, chromosomes), Mitochondria (powerhouse, ATP), Ribosomes (protein synthesis), ER (rough+smooth), Golgi body (packaging), Lysosomes (digestion, suicide bag), Chloroplasts (photosynthesis, in plants), Vacuoles (storage), Cell wall (plants+fungi, cellulose). Cell division: Mitosis (2 identical daughter cells, growth/replace) vs Meiosis (4 gametes, halved chromosomes, reproduction). DNA double helix (Watson & Crick 1953). RNA (single strand, transcription, translation). Genes: segments of DNA coding for proteins. Chromosomes: 23 pairs human (22 autosomes + 1 sex XX/XY).
Human Body:
Systems: Circulatory (heart 4 chambers: 2 atria+2 ventricles, blood vessels: artery/vein/capillary, blood: RBC/Hb, WBC/immunity, platelets/clotting, plasma). Respiratory (lungs, trachea, bronchi, alveoli, diaphragm, haemoglobin transports O₂, 12-16 breaths/min). Digestive (mouth→oesophagus→stomach→small intestine→large intestine→anus, accessory: liver (bile, largest gland), pancreas (enzymes+insulin), gall bladder). Excretory (kidneys 2: nephrons filter blood, ureter→bladder→urethra, urine: urea+water+salt, ~1.5L/day). Nervous (brain: cerebrum/intelligence, cerebellum/balance, medulla/vital functions, spinal cord: reflexes, nerves). Endocrine: pituitary (master gland), thyroid (metabolism), pancreas (insulin/glucagon), adrenal (adrenaline), gonads (testes/ovaries). Skeletal (206 bones, axial 80+appendicular 126, joints: ball-socket, hinge, pivot). Muscular (skeletal/voluntary, smooth/involuntary, cardiac/heart).
Sense Organs: Eye (vision, retina rods/b&w + cones/colour), Ear (hearing+balance, cochlea/auditory, semicircular canals/balance), Nose (smell, olfactory epithelium), Tongue (taste: sweet/salty/sour/bitter/umami, taste buds), Skin (touch, pain, pressure, temperature).
Common Diseases: Viral: COVID-19 (SARS-CoV-2), Flu (Influenza), HIV/AIDS, Hepatitis B/C, Dengue, Chikungunya, Measles, Polio, Rabies, Chickenpox. Bacterial: TB (Mycobacterium), Typhoid (Salmonella), Cholera (Vibrio cholerae), Tetanus (Clostridium), Pneumonia (Streptococcus), Leprosy (Mycobacterium leprae), Plague (Yersinia pestis). Protozoan: Malaria (Plasmodium, Anopheles mosquito), Amoebiasis (Entamoeba), Kala-azar (Leishmania). Fungal: Ringworm, Athlete's foot. Deficiency: Anaemia (iron), Goitre (iodine), Night blindness/keratomalacia (Vitamin A), Beriberi (B1), Pellagra (B3), Scurvy (C), Rickets/Osteomalacia (D). Lifestyle: Diabetes Type 2 (insulin resistance), Hypertension, Heart disease, Stroke, Cancer (uncontrolled cell division).
Vitamins & Minerals: A (retinol, milk/eggs/carrots - vision, immunity), B1 (thiamine, grains - nerve function), B2 (riboflavin, milk - skin), B3 (niacin, meat - energy), B5 (pantothenic, all foods - CoA), B6 (pyridoxine, chicken - metabolism), B7 (biotin, eggs - hair/nails), B9 (folic acid, leafy greens - RBC, pregnancy), B12 (cobalamin, animal products - nerve, RBC), C (ascorbic acid, citrus/fruits - immunity, collagen, antioxidant), D (calciferol, sunlight/fortified milk - calcium absorption, bones), E (tocopherol, nuts/oils - antioxidant), K (phylloquinone, greens - blood clotting). Minerals: Calcium (bones), Iron (Hb), Iodine (thyroid), Zinc (immunity), Magnesium (muscle), Potassium (heart), Sodium (nerve), Selenium (antioxidant), Phosphorus (energy), Fluoride (teeth).
Plant Biology: Photosynthesis: 6CO₂+6H₂O→C₆H₁₂O₆+6O₂ (chlorophyll, sunlight). Transpiration (water loss). Respiration (glucose breakdown). Tropisms: phototropism, geotropism. Hormones: auxin (growth), gibberellin (stem), cytokinin (cell division), abscisic acid (stress), ethylene (ripening). Plant Nutrition: macronutrients (N,P,K,Ca,Mg,S) & micronutrients (Fe,Zn,Mn,B,Cu,Mo,Cl). Crop types: cereals (rice/wheat/maize), pulses (gram/arhar/soybean), oilseeds (groundnut/mustard).
Biotechnology: Genetic engineering: recombinant DNA (rDNA) technology. CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing. Transgenic crops: Bt cotton (insect resistant, Cry genes from Bacillus thuringiensis), Golden Rice (beta-carotene modified), GM Mustard (Hybrid). GMO (Genetically Modified Organism). Hybridization vs Transgenic. Cloning: Dolly sheep (1996, Roslin). Stem cells (embryonic/adult). Gene therapy (correct defective genes). DNA fingerprinting (VNTRs, used in forensics). Monoclonal antibodies (COVID, cancer). Fermentation (yogurt, bread, cheese, beer, wine, vinegar). Bioremediation (oil spills, waste). Vaccines: inactivated/attenuated/mRNA (Pfizer, Moderna)/viral vector (Covishield). Biofuels: ethanol (sugarcane), biodiesel (jatropha), biogas (cow dung).
Environmental Science & Ecology: Ecosystem (producers + consumers + decomposers). Food chain → Food web. Energy flow: 10% rule (Lindeman). Biogeochemical cycles: Carbon, Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Water. Biodiversity: genetic, species, ecosystem. Biodiversity hotspots in India: Western Ghats, Eastern Himalayas, Indo-Burma. National Parks & Wildlife Sanctuaries. Endangered: Tiger, Elephant, Rhino, Great Indian Bustard, Lion-tailed Macaque, Gharial. Wildlife Protection Act 1972, Project Tiger 1973, Project Elephant 1992. Biosphere Reserves: Nilgiri (first 1986), Nanda Devi, Sundarbans, Gulf of Mannar. Botanical Gardens: howrah (oldest 1787, in India). IUCN Red List categories. Climate change impacts on biodiversity.
Indian Scientists & Contributions: C.V. Raman (Nobel 1930, Raman Effect scattering of light). S. Chandrasekhar (Nobel 1983, Chandrasekhar limit, white dwarfs). H.G. Khorana (Nobel 1968, genetic code). Venkatraman Ramakrishnan (Nobel 2009, ribosome structure). Satyendra Bose (Bose-Einstein condensation, Boson, Indian Statistical Institute). Meghnad Saha (ionization equation, Saha Institute). Vikram Sarabhai (father of Indian space programme, ISRO founding). Homi Bhabha (father of Indian nuclear programme, BARC). A.P.J. Abdul Kalam (ISRO, DRDO, Missile Man, President). J.C. Bose (plant electrophysiology, Crescograph, wireless pioneer). M.S. Swaminathan (father of Indian Green Revolution).
Nobel Prizes in Science: Physics: 1901 Röntgen (X-rays), 1905 Lenard (cathode rays), 1921 Einstein (photoelectric effect), 1932 Heisenberg (quantum), 1938 Fermi (neutron), 1957 Yang & Lee (parity), 1979 Salam/Weinberg/Glashow (electroweak), 2016 Thouless/Haldane/Kosterlitz (topology), 2017 Weiss/Barish/Thorne (gravitational waves), 2023 L'Huillier/Krausz/Agostini (attosecond physics). Chemistry: 1911 Curie (radium), 1931 Bergius/Bosch (coal hydrogenation), 1944 Hahn (fission), 1996 Curl/Kroto/Smalley (fullerenes), 2020 Charpentier/Doudna (CRISPR). Medicine: 1901 Behring (diphtheria), 1905 Koch (TB), 1928 Nicolle (typhus), 1945 Fleming/Chain/Florey (penicillin), 1953 Krebs (TCA cycle), 1962 Watson/Crick/Wilkins (DNA), 2008 zur Hausen (HPV), Barré-Sinoussi/Montagnier (HIV), 2020 Alter/Houghton/Rice (Hepatitis C).
Important Inventions: Wheel (~3500 BC), Printing Press (Gutenberg 1440), Telephone (Bell 1876), Light Bulb (Edison 1879), Radio (Marconi 1895), Television (Baird 1925), Transistor (Bardeen/Brattain/Shockley 1947), Computer (Babbage/ENIAC 1946), Microprocessor (Intel 1971), Internet (ARPANET 1969, Berners-Lee WWW 1989), Mobile Phone (Motorola DynaTAC 1973), Smartphone (iPhone 2007). Indian inventions: Binary zero (Aryabhata), Cataract surgery (Sushruta), Chess (Gupta), Cotton cultivation, Shampoo, Surgery, Yoga, Plastic surgery (Sushruta). Indian Space Research: Chandrayaan-1 (2008 discovered water on moon), Chandrayaan-2 (2019 orbiter working), Chandrayaan-3 (2023 landed near lunar South Pole, first to do so). Mangalyaan/MOM (2014 cheapest Mars mission). Aditya L1 (2023 solar mission). Gaganyaan (2025 human spaceflight planned). XPoSat (2024 X-ray polarimetry).

environment.title: Environment & Ecology
environment.content:
Environment & Ecology Basics:
Ecology Concepts: Ecology = study of interaction between organisms & environment. Ecosystem = community + abiotic factors. Components: Biotic (producers, consumers, decomposers) & Abiotic (sunlight, water, soil, temp). Food chain: Trophic levels, 10% energy transfer (Lindeman's law). Food web: interconnected food chains. Ecological pyramids: Pyramid of numbers, biomass, energy (always upright). Biome: large community of plants/animals in a climate zone (tropical rainforest, taiga, tundra, desert, grassland). Biogeochemical cycles: Carbon (photosynthesis + respiration), Nitrogen (fixation by Rhizobium, nitrification, denitrification), Phosphorus (no atmospheric phase), Water cycle (evaporation, condensation, precipitation).
Biodiversity: Genetic (genes within species), Species (variety of species), Ecosystem (diversity of habitats). Biodiversity hotspots: 36 globally, 4 in India - Western Ghats, Eastern Himalayas, Indo-Burma, Sundaland. Endemic species: found only in one region (Lion-tailed Macaque, Nilgiri Tahr, Sangai deer). Keystone species: disproportionately large effect on ecosystem (tiger, sea otter, elephants). Flagship species: charismatic to raise conservation support (tiger). Umbrella species: protection protects many others (elephant). Indicator species: sensitive to environmental change (lichen, frogs). IUCN Red List categories: Extinct (EX), Extinct in Wild (EW), Critically Endangered (CR), Endangered (EN), Vulnerable (VU), Near Threatened (NT), Least Concern (LC). Last 3 categories in India: Cheetah (extinct 1952, reintroduced 2023), Great Indian Bustard (CR), Bengal Tiger (EN), Asiatic Lion (EN), Snow Leopard (VU), One-horned Rhino (VU), Red Panda (EN).
Forests & Wildlife Conservation: Forest Survey of India (FSI) biennial ISFR report. Forest cover ~24.62% of India (2025 ISFR). Very dense forest (canopy >70%), moderately dense (40-70%), open (10-40%). Top states by forest cover: MP, Arunachal, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Maharashtra. National Parks (106+ as of 2026): Jim Corbett (first, 1936), Kaziranga (rhino), Gir (Asiatic lion), Sundarbans (tiger + mangrove), Periyar (elephant), Ranthambore (tiger). Wildlife Sanctuaries (573+). Tiger Reserves (54): Project Tiger 1973, NTCA (National Tiger Conservation Authority). Elephant Reserves (33): Project Elephant 1992. Biosphere Reserves (18): Nilgiri (first, 1986), Nanda Devi, Sundarbans, Gulf of Mannar, Great Nicobar, Simlipal, Achanakmar-Amarkantak, etc. Bird Sanctuaries: Bharatpur (Keoladeo), Chilika (Nalaban), Ranganathittu. Wetlands (Ramsar sites): 85+ in India — Chilika, Keoladeo, Wular, Loktak, Sambhar, Kolleru, Vembanad, Ashtamudi, Bhitarkanika, Pangong Tso, Tso Moriri, etc. Ramsar Convention 1971 (Iran).
Pollution & Environmental Issues: Air: PM2.5/PM10, SO2, NOx, CO, Ozone, AQI (0-500, 6 categories). National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS). NCAP (National Clean Air Programme 2019): reduce PM by 40% by 2026 in 131 non-attainment cities. Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) for Delhi-NCR. Water: BOD (dissolved oxygen demand), COD, eutrophication (algae bloom from N/P), heavy metals. CPCB (Central Pollution Control Board). Ganga Action Plan (1985), Namami Gange (2014), NMCG (National Mission for Clean Ganga). Soil: pesticides, insecticides, herbicides, microplastics, heavy metals. Noise: >55 dB daytime residential, >45 dB night. Climate Change: Greenhouse gases: CO2 (major), CH4, N2O, HFCs, SF6. Global Warming Potential (GWP) - CO2=1, CH4=25, N2O=298. IPCC reports (Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change). UNFCCC (1992), Kyoto Protocol (1997, binding targets for developed), Paris Agreement (2015, all countries, NDCs). India's INDC: 33-35% emissions intensity reduction by 2030 vs 2005. Updated NDC 2022: 500 GW non-fossil by 2030, 50% renewable, 1B ton carbon sink. National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC 2008): 8 National Missions (Solar, Enhanced Energy Efficiency, Water, Himalayan Ecosystem, Green India, Sustainable Agriculture, Strategic Knowledge, Health). Ozone depletion: CFCs, Montreal Protocol 1987, Kigali Amendment (2016) on HFCs. Ozone hole over Antarctica. Environmental Acts: Wildlife Protection Act 1972 (6 schedules), Forest Conservation Act 1980 (diversion of forest land), Environment Protection Act 1986 (umbrella legislation), Air Act 1981, Water Act 1974, Biological Diversity Act 2002, National Green Tribunal Act 2010.
Important International Summits: Stockholm Conference 1972 (UN Conference on Human Environment). Rio Earth Summit 1992 (UNCED, Agenda 21, Forest Principles, Biodiversity Convention, Climate Convention). Johannesburg Summit 2002 (WSSD, sustainable development). Rio+20 2012 (The Future We Want, SDGs). COP (Conference of Parties) annual climate summits: COP3 Kyoto (1997), COP15 Copenhagen (2009), COP21 Paris (2015), COP26 Glasgow (2021, Article 6 finalized). Montreal Protocol 1987 (ozone). Cartagena Protocol 2000 (biosafety). Nagoya Protocol 2010 (access to genetic resources). Minamata Convention 2013 (mercury). Sendai Framework 2015 (disaster risk reduction).
Environmental Organisations: UNEP (Nairobi, 1972). WWF (1961, panda logo). IUCN (Gland, Switzerland, 1948). IPCC (1988, climate science). WMO (weather, climate). Greenpeace (1971, activist). CSE (Centre for Science & Environment, Delhi, Anil Agarwal). TERI (Energy & Resources Institute, Delhi). BNHS (Bombay Natural History Society, 1883). Wildlife Institute of India (Dehradun). Indian Institute of Forest Management (Bhopal).
Environmental Issues in India: Bhopal Gas Tragedy (1984, MIC leak, Union Carbide). Narmada Bachao Andolan (dam displacement). POSCO steel plant (Odisha). Sterlite Copper (Tuticorin, 2018). Delhi air pollution (stubble burning + vehicles). Cauvery water dispute. Yamuna pollution (sewage + industrial effluents). Sand mining (illegal, river ecology). Plastic waste management (phase-out single use plastic 2022). E-waste management rules. Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) 2019 notification. Western Ghats (Gadgil & Kasturirangan reports).
Important Environmental Terms: Carbon footprint, Water footprint, Ecological footprint, Carrying capacity, Eutrophication, Biomagnification (DDT in food chain), Bioaccumulation, Ozone hole, Acid rain (pH<5.6), Smog (classical + photochemical), Green building, Carbon credit, Carbon neutral, Net zero, Carbon sequestration, Carbon sink, Carbon source, Afforestation, Reforestation, Deforestation, Desertification, Land degradation, Sustainable development, Circular economy, Green GDP, ESG, Greenwashing, Climate resilience, Adaptation, Mitigation, Blue carbon, REDD+ (Reducing Emissions from Deforestation), REDD+ (UN programme), CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism by EU), Just Transition, Loss & Damage fund (COP27).
Renewable Energy in India: Target 500 GW non-fossil by 2030. Solar: Bhadla (Rajasthan, 2.25 GW), Pavagada (Karnataka, 2 GW), Kurnool (AP, 1 GW). Wind: Tamil Nadu (Muppandal), Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka. PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli (rooftop solar, 2024). National Green Hydrogen Mission (5 MMT by 2030). Biofuels: ethanol blending target 20% by 2025 (achieved ~15% in 2024). Waste-to-energy plants. Small hydro, tidal, geothermal (small scale). ISA (International Solar Alliance, launched by India & France at COP21, HQ Gurugram).

culture.title: Indian Art & Culture
culture.content:
Indian Paintings:
Prehistoric & Rock Art: Bhimbetka (MP, UNESCO, 30,000 yrs old, 700+ rock shelters). Also at Adamgarh, Pachmarhi. Mural Paintings: Ajanta Caves (Buddhist, 2ndC BC-7thC AD, Jataka tales). Ellora Caves (Buddhist-Hindu-Jain, 7th-10thC). Bagh Caves (MP, 5th-6thC). Sittanavasal (TN, Jain, 7thC, fresco). Lepakshi (AP, 16thC, Vijayanagara). Mattancherry Palace (Kerala, 16thC, Dutch + Kerala style). Miniature Paintings: Pala School (eastern India, 8th-12thC, Buddhist palm leaf manuscripts). Jain School (Gujarat/Rajasthan, 12th-16thC, Kalpasutra). Mughal School (Babur-Akbar-Jahangir-Shah Jahan-Aurangzeb, Persian influence, Hamzanama, Tuti-nama). Rajasthani/Rajput Schools: Mewar (Rana Kumbha, Sahibdin), Bundi, Kota, Jaipur, Marwar, Kishangarh (Bani Thani, Nihal Chand), Alwar. Pahari Schools: Basohli (bold colours, strong facial), Guler, Kangra (soft, romantic, Nayika bheda, Nainsukh, Manku). Folk Paintings: Madhubani/Mithila (Bihar, women artists, ritual motifs). Warli (Maharashtra, tribal, white on mud, stick figures). Pattachitra (Odisha, cloth/coconut leaf, Jagannath themes). Pattachitra (Bengal, Kalighat style, bold lines). Gond (MP, tribal, dotted patterns, Jangarh Singh Shyam). Bhil (MP/Gujarat, bright dots, Pithora style). Kalamkari (AP, hand-painted/block-printed, temple cloth). Saura (Odisha, stick figures, wall paintings). Phad (Rajasthan, scroll paintings of folk deities Pabuji, Devnarayan). Pichwai (Rajasthan, Krishna scenes, cloth hangings). Thanjavur (Tamil Nadu, gold foil, embedded gems, gods). Cheriyal Scrolls (Telangana, story-telling scrolls).
Indian Music:
Hindustani Classical (North India): Origins from Sama Veda. 10 Thaats (scales, Bhatkhande). Gharanas: Gwalior (oldest), Agra, Jaipur, Kirana, Patiala, Rampur, Maihar (Allauddin Khan, Ravi Shankar). Carnatic Music (South India): 72 Melakarta ragas. Trinity of Carnatic: Tyagaraja (composer, Pancharatna Kritis), Muthuswami Dikshitar, Syama Sastri. Purandara Dasa (father of Carnatic music, Mayamalavagowla raga). Instruments: Veena (Rudra, Saraswati, Vichitra, string), Sitar (Ravi Shankar, plucked string), Sarod (Amjad Ali Khan, fretless, 25 strings), Santoor (Shivkumar Sharma, hammered dulcimer), Shehnai (Ustad Bismillah Khan, wind, auspicious), Flute/Bansuri (Pt. Hariprasad Chaurasia, H. Pannalal Ghosh), Harmonium (Bhatkhande introduced, controversial). Percussion: Tabla (Zakir Hussain, Allah Rakha), Pakhawaj (ancient, Dhrupad), Mridangam (Carnatic drum), Ghatam (clay pot, Carnatic), Kanjira (tambourine), Dhol (Punjabi, Bihu), Dholak (folk), Nagara (processional). Vocal forms: Hindustani: Dhrupad (oldest, slow majestic), Khayal (romantic, lyrical, Amir Khusrau), Thumri (semi-classical, love), Dadra, Tappa (fast), Tarana, Ghazal (Urdu poetry). Carnatic: Varnam (composition for practice), Kriti (Tyagaraja/Muthuswami), Tillana (pure rhythm), Ragam Tanam Pallavi (RTP, complex improvisation).
Indian Dance:
Classical Dances (8 Sangeet Natak Akademi recognized): Bharatanatyam (TN, oldest, Nataraja pose, Padam/Varnam/Tillana). Kathak (UP/dance + footwork, spins/Chakkars). Kathakali (Kerala/dance drama, elaborate makeup+masks, Mudras facial expressions, green/red/black). Odissi (Odisha/tribhanga posture, sculpturesque, Mangalacharan). Kuchipudi (AP/brass plate dance, Tarangam, Kuravanji). Manipuri (Manipur/smooth graceful, Ras Lila, alap, Chali). Mohiniyattam (Kerala/solo woman, graceful swaying). Sattriya (Assam/monastic, 15thC, Srimanta Sankardev). Folk Dances: Bhangra (Punjab/harvest, harvest), Giddha (Punjab/female), Garba (Gujarat/navratri circle dance), Dandiya (Gujarat/stick), Bihu (Assam/spring), Ghoomar (Rajasthan/tribal, Bhil), Kalbelia (Rajasthan/snake charmer, UNESCO), Lavani (Maharashtra/folk + sensuous), Powada (Maharashtra/martial ballads), Chhau (WB/Odisha/Jharkhand/mask dance), Nautanki (UP/song-drama), Yakshagana (Karnataka/folk theatre), Theyyam (Kerala/ritual, gods possessed), Rouff (Kashmir/Sufi), Bardo Chham (Arunachal/tribal), Hojagiri (Tripura/balance pots), Karakattam (TN/water pot), Oyilattam (TN/folk), Bamboo dance (Mizoram/Cheraw), Karma (MP/Jharkhand/tribal).
Indian Theatre: Natyashastra by Bharata Muni (ancient treatise, 36 chapters, 8 rasas + Shanta). Traditional forms: Ramlila (Rama story, major dramas). Raslila (Krishna/Krishna). Nautanki (UP/dance-opera, colourful). Swang (Haryana/Punjab, dialogue songs). Bhavai (Gujarat/satirical, balancing pots). Tamasha (Maharashtra/folk, Lavani + drama). Therukoothu (Tamil street theatre). Bhand Pather (Kashmir/folk plays). Jatra (West Bengal, Odisha, Assam/folk opera, loud music, melodrama). Maach (MP/singing+acting). Dashavatar (Konkan, 10 avatars). Kudiyattam (Kerala/Sanskrit, UNESCO, oldest surviving). Kathputli (Rajasthan/puppetry). Shadow puppetry (Tholu Bommalata AP, Togalu Gombeya Karnataka). Puppet traditions: string (Kathputli), shadow (Tholu Bommalata), glove (Bahurupi), rod (Putul Nautch).
Indian Architecture:
Ancient & Classical: Indus Valley (grid planning, Great Bath, burnt bricks). Mauryan (Ashokan pillars, stupas - Sanchi, Barabar caves). Shunga (gateways, railing). Satavahana (Amaravati stupa). Gupta (temple architecture beginning: Dashavatara Temple Deogarh, Bhitargaon). Nagara Style (North): curvilinear spire (shikhara), garbhagriha, mandapa. Khajuraho (Chandela, Kandariya Mahadev), Sun Temple Konark (Odisha, chariot, 12 wheels), Lingaraja Bhubaneswar, Jagannath Puri. Dravidian Style (South): stepped pyramid vimana, gopuram - huge gateway. Pallava (Mahabalipuram rathas/caves). Chola (Brihadeeswara Tanjore, 65m vimana). Pandya (Meenakshi Madurai). Vijayanagara (Hampi, Vitthala temple, stone chariot). Nayaka (additional gopuram corridors). Vesara Style (Deccan): hybrid Nagara+Dravidian. Chalukya (Pattadakal, Aihole 125 temples, Badami cave temples). Rashtrakuta (Ellora Kailasa - monolithic rock-cut, 8thC). Hoysala (Belur Chennakeshava, Halebidu, star-shaped platform). Indo-Islamic/Indo-Saracenic: Delhi Sultanate: Qutb Minar, Alai Darwaza, Jamali Kamali. Mughal: Humayun's Tomb (Indo-Persian, charbagh), Taj Mahal (marble inlay, symmetry), Red Fort, Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri (Buland Darwaza, Panch Mahal). Deccan style: Gol Gumbaz Bijapur (whispering gallery, 44m dome), Charminar, Bidar fort. Provincial: Jaunpur, Gujarat (Jama Masjid Ahmedabad). Modern: Lutyens' Delhi (Rashtrapati Bhavan, Parliament, India Gate). Corbusier (Chandigarh Capitol). Charles Correa (BMC Mumbai, Jawahar Kala Kendra, Bharat Bhavan). Laurie Baker (low-cost brick architecture). Lotus Temple (Bahai, Fariborz Sahba, 1986).
Indian Handicrafts & Textiles: Banarasi silk (UP, gold/silver zari). Kanchipuram silk (TN, pure mulberry silk). Phulkari (Punjab, floral embroidery). Chikankari (Lucknow, white thread on muslin). Kasuti (Karnataka, embroidery). Kutch embroidery (Gujarat, mirror work). Patola (Gujarat, double ikat). Pashmina (Kashmir, cashmere wool). Kalamkari (AP, hand-painted). Bandhani/Bandhej (Rajasthan, tie-dye). Ikat (Odisha, Telangana, tie-dye warp/weft). Chamba rumal (HP, embroidery). Chanderi (MP, silk+cotton). Maheshwari (MP, stripes/checks). Tussar silk (Jharkhand, Bihar). Muga silk (Assam, golden). Cane & bamboo (NE, traditional). Bidriware (Karnataka, metal inlay). Dhokra (Bengal/Odisha, lost wax casting). Channapatna toys (Karnataka, lacquer, wood). Saharanpur wood carving (UP). Blue pottery (Jaipur). Warli (tribal painting on cloth).
UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage from India: Kutiyattam (2008). Vedic chanting (2008). Ramlila (2008). Chhau dance (2010). Kalbelia (2010). Buddhist chanting (2012). Sankirtana (Manipur, 2013). Yoga (2016). Nawrouz (2016). Kumbh Mela (2017). Durga Puja (2021). Garba (2023).
Cultural Institutions in India: Sangeet Natak Akademi (1952, classical dance/music/theatre). Lalit Kala Akademi (1954, visual arts). Sahitya Akademi (1954, literature). National School of Drama (1959, Delhi). National Museum (New Delhi). National Gallery of Modern Art (Delhi/Bengaluru/Mumbai). Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA, Delhi). Centre for Cultural Resources and Training (CCRT). Archaeological Survey of India (ASI, 1861, protects monuments).
Languages in India: 8th Schedule: 22 official languages. Classical languages: Tamil (2004), Sanskrit (2005), Telugu (2008), Kannada (2008), Malayalam (2013), Odia (2014). Oldest: Tamil (2,000+ years). Most spoken: Hindi (43.63% as per 2011 census). India linguistic diversity: 1,369 mother tongues (Census 2011). Language families: Indo-Aryan (majority), Dravidian (South), Austroasiatic (Munda), Tibeto-Burman (NE).
Religious Diversity in India: Hinduism (largest, 80%+). Islam (2nd, ~14%). Christianity (3rd, ~2.3%). Sikhism (~1.7%). Buddhism (~0.7%). Jainism (~0.4%). Zoroastrianism/Parsi (declining). Judaism (small Jewish population - Cochin, Mumbai, NE). Bahai faith (Lotus Temple). Adivasi/Sarna/Donyi-Polo (indigenous faiths). Places: Char Dham (Badrinath, Dwarka, Puri, Rameswaram). 12 Jyotirlingas (Somnath, Kedarnath, Kashi Vishwanath, etc.). Golden Temple (Amritsar, Sikh). Ajmer Sharif (Sufi). St Thomas Mount (Chennai, Christianity's Indian arrival).
Fairs & Festivals of India: Diwali (festival of lights, Oct-Nov). Holi (colours, Mar). Dussehra (Rama-Ravana battle, Oct). Durga Puja (WB, grand pandals, Oct). Eid-ul-Fitr (end of Ramadan). Eid-ul-Adha (sacrifice). Guru Nanak Jayanti (Gurupurab, Nov). Christmas (Dec 25). Pongal (Tamil harvest, Jan). Makar Sankranti (kite flying, Jan). Baisakhi (Punjab harvest, Apr). Onam (Kerala harvest, Aug-Sep). Navratri (9 nights, Oct). Ganesh Chaturthi (MH, Sep-Oct). Janmashtami (Krishna birthday, Aug). Mahashivaratri (Shiva night, Feb-Mar). Rath Yatra (Puri, chariot, Jul). Kumbh Mela (largest pilgrimage, 4 locations: Allahabad, Haridwar, Ujjain, Nashik, every 12 years, 2019 largest gathering ever). Hemis Gompa (Ladakh, Buddhist). Losar (Tibetan New Year, Feb). Hornbill Festival (Nagaland, Dec).

computers.title: Computer & IT
computers.content:
Computer Basics:
Computer Generations: 1st (1940-56: Vacuum tubes, ENIAC, UNIVAC, punch cards). 2nd (1956-63: Transistors, smaller, faster). 3rd (1964-71: Integrated Circuits ICs, IBM 360). 4th (1971-present: Microprocessors, VLSI, PCs). 5th (AI, quantum, parallel processing, ULSI).
Hardware Components: CPU (Central Processing Unit - ALU + Control Unit + Registers). Motherboard (main circuit board, connects all components). RAM (Random Access Memory, volatile, program data). ROM (Read Only Memory, non-volatile, boot instructions, BIOS/UEFI). Hard Disk Drive (HDD, magnetic, slower, high capacity). Solid State Drive (SSD, flash, faster, no moving parts). GPU (Graphics Processing Unit - displays visuals). PSU (Power Supply Unit). Cooling fan/heat sink. Ports: USB (A/B/C), HDMI, VGA, DisplayPort, Ethernet (RJ45), Audio jack, Thunderbolt. Input: Keyboard, Mouse, Touchpad, Touchscreen, Scanner, Microphone, Webcam, Barcode reader, Biometric sensor. Output: Monitor (LED/LCD/OLED), Printer (Laser/Inkjet/Dot matrix), Speaker, Projector, Headphones. Storage units: Bit (0/1), Byte = 8 bits, KB (1024B), MB (1024KB), GB (1024MB), TB (1024GB), PB (1024TB).
Software: System Software (OS, Device Drivers, Utilities). Application Software (MS Office, Browser, Games). Operating Systems: Windows (Microsoft), macOS (Apple), Linux (open source: Ubuntu, Fedora, Debian, Android based on Linux). Programming Languages: Machine (binary), Assembly (mnemonics), High-Level (C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, Ruby, PHP, C#, Swift, Kotlin, Go, Rust). Compiler (all at once) vs Interpreter (line by line). Database: MySQL, Oracle, PostgreSQL, MongoDB. DBMS, RDBMS, SQL. Open source: code publicly available (Linux, Firefox, Python). Proprietary: owned (Windows, MS Office, Photoshop).
Internet & Networking: Network types: LAN (local, office), WAN (wide, internet), MAN (city), PAN (personal). Internet: global network of networks. WWW (World Wide Web, Tim Berners-Lee 1989, CERN). ISP (Internet Service Provider). IP Address (IPv4: 32-bit, 4.3B addresses, e.g., 192.168.1.1; IPv6: 128-bit). Domain Name System (DNS - translates domain to IP). URL (Uniform Resource Locator). HTTP/HTTPS (HyperText Transfer Protocol, HTTPS = secure with SSL/TLS). FTP (File Transfer Protocol). SMTP/POP3/IMAP (email protocols). TCP/IP (Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol - backbone of internet). Router (directs traffic), Modem (modulates/demodulates), Switch, Hub, Bridge, Gateway. Wi-Fi (Wireless Fidelity, IEEE 802.11). Bluetooth (short-range wireless). Ethernet (wired). Fiber optic (light signals, high speed). 5G (5th generation cellular, high speed low latency). Satellite internet (Starlink, VSAT).
Cybersecurity: Virus (self-replicating malicious code). Worm (spreads without file). Trojan (disguised as legitimate). Ransomware (encrypts data, demands payment). Phishing (fake emails/sites to steal info). Spyware (steals data without knowledge). Adware (unwanted ads). Malware (malicious software). Firewall (blocks unauthorized access). Antivirus (detects/removes malware). Encryption (scrambles data, AES, RSA). VPN (Virtual Private Network - encrypts connection). Password management (strong, unique passwords). 2FA/MFA (Two-Factor/Multi-Factor Authentication). Biometric (fingerprint, face recognition). OWASP Top 10 (web app vulnerabilities). SQL injection, XSS (Cross-Site Scripting), CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery), DDoS (Distributed Denial of Service - floods server). Zero-day exploit. Social engineering (human manipulation). Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attack. Ethical hacking (authorized penetration testing). CERT-In (Indian Computer Emergency Response Team, nodal agency for cyber security). IT Act 2000 (India's cyber law, amended 2008). Personal Data Protection Bill (2023).
Important IT Terms & Concepts: AI (Artificial Intelligence - machine mimics human intelligence). ML (Machine Learning - learns from data). Deep Learning (neural networks). ChatGPT (OpenAI, LLM). Generative AI (produces content: text, image, music). Cloud Computing (SaaS/PaaS/IaaS - AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Salesforce). Big Data (large datasets, Hadoop, Spark). IoT (Internet of Things - smart devices connected). Blockchain (distributed ledger, Bitcoin). Cryptocurrency (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Dogecoin). Quantum Computing (qubits, superposition). Virtual Reality (VR - immersive). Augmented Reality (AR - overlay). Mixed Reality (MR). Cryptography (encryption, decryption). Digital Signature (authenticates sender). CAPTCHA (bot detection). QR Code (Quick Response). RFID (Radio-Frequency Identification). NFC (Near Field Communication). GPS (Global Positioning System). GIS (Geographic Information System).
Indian IT Industry: TCS (Tata Consultancy Services, largest). Infosys (Bangalore). Wipro (Bangalore). HCL Technologies (Noida). Tech Mahindra (Pune). LTI Mindtree. India's IT sector ~$250B (2024). Silicon Valley of India: Bangalore. Cyber City: Gurugram. IT hubs: Hyderabad, Pune, Chennai, Noida, Mumbai, Kolkata. Software Technology Parks of India (STPI). NASSCOM (trade association for IT-BPM). Digital India programme (2015). Aadhaar (biometric ID, 1.3B+ enrollments). UPI (Unified Payments Interface, 11B+ transactions/month). polity.title: Indian Polity
polity.content:
Indian Parliament:
Structure: Bicameral: Lok Sabha (House of the People, 543 elected + 2 Anglo-Indian nominated = max 550, 5-year term) + Rajya Sabha (Council of States, 233 elected + 12 nominated by President = 245, 6-year term, 1/3 retire every 2 years). Lok Sabha Speaker (Om Birla). Rajya Sabha Chairman (Vice President of India). Deputy Speaker, Deputy Chairman. Sessions: Budget (Feb-May), Monsoon (Jul-Sep), Winter (Nov-Dec). Special sessions. Prorogation, Adjournment, Adjournment sine die, Dissolution (only LS). Quorum: 1/10th of total members. Legislative Process: Bill types: Ordinary, Money (Art 110), Financial, Constitutional Amendment. Passage through both houses + President assent. Money Bill only in LS, RS can delay 14 days. Joint sitting (Art 108) for deadlock (called by President). Only 3 joint sittings held: Dowry Prohibition 1961, Banking Service Commission 1978, POTA 2002. Committees: Standing/Ad hoc. Financial: Public Accounts (PAC, 22 members, 1 yr), Estimates (30 members), Committee on Public Undertakings (22). Departmentally Related Standing Committees (DRSCs, 24). Other: Business Advisory, Privileges, Rules, Petitions, Private Members, Papers Laid, Government Assurances, Subordinate Legislation, Official Language, Ethics, Library. Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC, ad hoc).
Constitutional Bodies: Election Commission (Art 324, CEC + 2 ECs). UPSC (Art 315-323, Chairman + 10 members). SPSC. Finance Commission (Art 280, Chairman + 4 members, every 5 years). CAG (Art 148, 6-year term). Attorney General (Art 76, 65 yr age, top law officer). Advocate General (Art 165, state level). National Commission for SCs (Art 338). National Commission for STs (Art 338A). National Commission for Backward Classes (Art 338B, 102nd Amendment 2018). National Commission for Linguistic Minorities (Art 350B). Official Language Commission. Commission to examine conditions of Anglo-Indians. Non-Constitutional Bodies: NITI Aayog (2015, replaced Planning Commission). National Human Rights Commission (NHRC, 1993, Paris Principles). National Commission for Women (NCW, 1992). National Commission for Minorities (1992). National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR, 2007). CVC (Central Vigilance Commission, 1964 statutory 2003). CBI (Central Bureau of Investigation, 1963, Delhi Special Police Establishment Act). Competition Commission of India (CCI, 2003). SEBI (1992). TRAI (1997). IRDAI (1999). NGT (2010). Central Information Commission (CIC, 2005). State Information Commission. Lokpal (2013, anti-corruption ombudsman at centre, Chairman + 8 members). Lokayukta (state level). Comptroller & Auditor General (CAG): Art 148. Appointed by President for 6 yrs or until 65. Guardian of public purse. Audits all govt accounts. Reports to President/Governor. Known as "watchdog of Indian democracy". Cannot be removed except on proved misbehaviour/incapacity (same as SC judge removal).
Council of Ministers: Article 74-75. PM appointed by President. Ministers on PM advice. Cabinet (senior ministers), Ministers of State (independent charge/attached), Deputy Ministers. Total ministers cannot exceed 15% of LS strength. Cabinet Committees: Political Affairs (all senior ministers, highest), Economic Affairs, Security, Appointments, Parliamentary Affairs, etc. Cabinet Secretary (top civil servant, heads Cabinet Secretariat). Prime Minister: Head of govt, real executive. Appoints Council of Ministers. Presides over Cabinet. Leader of LS/RS. Article 78: PM to communicate all decisions to President. Oath of office & secrecy. Salary & perks under PM Act. No fixed term (during pleasure of President).
President of India: Article 52-62. Head of State, formal executive. Elected by electoral college (MPs + MLAs). Single transferable vote. Term 5 years. Can be removed by impeachment (Art 61) for violation of Constitution. Eligible if 35+ yrs, qualified for LS. Oath by CJI. Powers: Executive (appoints PM/ministers/CEC/CAG/Judges/Governors etc.), Legislative (summons parliament, address, dissolve LS, promulgate ordinances Art 123), Financial (money bill recommendation), Judicial (pardon Art 72), Military (supreme commander), Diplomatic, Emergency (Arts 352/356/360). Vice President: Art 63-71. Ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha. Elected by both houses (MPs). Term 5 years. Acts as President when vacancy. 35+ yrs, qualified for RS. Can be removed by RS resolution + LS agreement.
Supreme Court & Judiciary: Art 124-147. Supreme Court (1 CJI + 33 judges = 34 total). Appointed by President. CJI on seniority. Retirement 65 yrs. Removal by impeachment (Art 124(4)): proved misbehaviour/incapacity, passed by 2/3 of both houses. High Courts: 25 HCs (including common HCs). Retirement 62 yrs. Subordinate courts: District & Sessions courts. SC Powers: Original (Art 131, Centre-State/Inter-State disputes), Appellate (constitutional/civil/criminal special leave), Advisory (Art 143, President consultation), Review (Art 137, of own judgment), Contempt (Art 129), Judicial Review (test laws for constitutional validity). Writs (Art 32 for SC, Art 226 for HC): Habeas Corpus (produce body), Mandamus (command), Prohibition (prohibit), Quo Warranto (by what authority), Certiorari (quash order). Public Interest Litigation (PIL, since 1980s). Collegium system for judge appointments. NJAC struck down (2015). Article 144: all authorities to act in aid of SC.
Governor: Art 153-162. Appointed by President. Term 5 years (can be removed earlier). Executive head of state. Discretionary powers. Can reserve bill for President. Appoints CM & ministers. Can recommend President's Rule (Art 356). Eligible if 35+ yrs. No security of tenure. Not answerable to any court for exercise of powers. Can grant pardons under Art 161. Chief Minister: Real executive of state. Leader of majority party in legislative assembly. Appointed by Governor. Council of Ministers on CM advice. State Legislature: Unicameral (Legislative Assembly) or Bicameral (Assembly + Legislative Council, 6 states: AP, Telangana, UP, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka). Vidhan Sabha: max 500, min 60. Vidhan Parishad (Council): max 1/3 of Assembly, min 40.
Emergency Provisions: Art 352 (National Emergency): war/external aggression/armed rebellion, "internal disturbance" replaced by "armed rebellion" through 44th Amendment. Effects: FRs suspended (Art 19 automatically, others by order), Centre controls states, LS term extended. 3 times imposed: 1962 (China war), 1971 (Pakistan war), 1975-77 (internal disturbance). Art 356 (President's Rule/State Emergency): failure of constitutional machinery in state. Governor reports. LS approves within 2 months. Max 3 years (1 yr ordinary + 6 months + 6 months with conditions). Most controversial provision. Used 130+ times. Art 360 (Financial Emergency): never imposed. Amendment Procedure: Art 368. Simple majority vs special majority vs special majority + 50% state ratification. Basic Structure Doctrine (Kesavananda Bharati 1973): cannot destroy basic features (parliamentary supremacy, secularism, federalism, judicial review, FRs, etc.).
Centre-State Relations: Legislative (Art 245-255): 3 lists - Union (100 subjects), State (61), Concurrent (52). Residuary powers with Centre (Art 248). Administrative (Art 256-263): Centre gives directions to states. Inter-State Council (Art 263). All India Services (IAS/IPS/IFS, Art 312). Financial (Art 264-293): FC grants, GST, borrowing, tax sharing. Federal vs Unitary: India is federal with unitary bias ("Union of States" Art 1). Single Constitution, single citizenship, integrated judiciary, all-India services, emergency provisions tilt towards Centre. Local Self-Government: Panchayats (73rd Amendment 1992, Part IX, Art 243-243O, 29 subjects in 11th Schedule). Municipalities (74th Amendment 1992, Part IXA, Art 243P-243ZG, 18 subjects in 12th Schedule).
Important Doctrines: Basic Structure (Kesavananda 1973). Eclipse (existing laws inconsistent with FRs become dormant). Severability (invalid part severed if rest operative). Waiver (fundamental right cannot be waived). Pith & Substance (look at true nature of law). Colourable Legislation (cannot do indirectly what is prohibited). Harmonious Construction (interpret harmoniously). Prospective Overruling (Golaknath 1967). Occupied Field (if Centre covers a subject, state cannot). Repugnancy (if state law conflicts with central law, central prevails).
Important Constitutional Amendments: 1st (1951, land reforms, FRs restrictions), 7th (1956, states reorganization), 24th (1971, Parliament power to amend FRs), 25th (1971, property rights curtailment), 42nd (1976 mini-Constitution: added Fundamental Duties, Secularism, Socialism, 1975-77 emergency effects), 44th (1978: right to property deleted from FRs, emergency safeguards), 52nd (1985, anti-defection), 61st (1989, voting age 21 to 18), 73rd & 74th (1992, Panchayats & Municipalities), 86th (2002, RTE Art 21A), 91st (2003, total ministers limit 15%), 97th (2011, cooperative societies), 100th (2015, India-Bangladesh land boundary), 101st (2016, GST), 102nd (2018, NCBC constitutional), 103rd (2019, EWS reservation 10%), 105th (2021, states power to identify OBC), 106th (2023, 33% women reservation in LS & state assemblies).
Important Parliamentary Terms: Starred Question (oral answer + supplementaries), Unstarred (written answer), Short Notice (urgent, less than 10 days). Zero Hour (after question hour, without prior notice). Half-an-hour discussion (matter of urgent public importance). Adjournment Motion (interruption, serious matter). Censure Motion (against minister/whole council). No-Confidence Motion (remove Council of Ministers, LS only). Confidence Motion (prove majority). Calling Attention. Privilege Motion (breach of privilege). Point of Order (rule violation). Resolution (express opinion). Cut Motion (reduce expenditure). Guillotine (undiscussed demands passed). Closure (end debate). Whip (party direction).
Constitutional Posts — Key Persons (as of 2026): President: Droupadi Murmu. Vice President: Jagdeep Dhankhar. PM: Narendra Modi. CJI: Sanjiv Khanna. LS Speaker: Om Birla. RS Chairman: VP Jagdeep Dhankhar. Attorney General: R. Venkataramani. CEC: Rajiv Kumar. CAG: K. Sanjay Murthy. Chairpersons: NCSC (Kishor Makwana), NCST (Anju Bala), NCBC (Bhagwan Lal Sahni), NCW (Rekha Sharma), NCPCR (Priyank Kanoongo), CIC (Heeralal Samariya), NHRC (Justice Arun Kumar Mishra).

personalities.title: Famous Personalities
personalities.content:
National Leaders & Freedom Fighters:
Mahatma Gandhi (1869-1948): Father of Nation. Birth Oct 2. Law in London. Satyagraha in South Africa (1893-1914). Champaran (1917 - indigo), Kheda (1918), Ahmedabad mill strike (1918). Non-Cooperation (1920), Dandi March (1930), Quit India (1942). Assassinated Jan 30, 1948 by Nathuram Godse. Autobiography: "The Story of My Experiments with Truth". Jawaharlal Nehru (1889-1964): First PM (1947-64). Discovery of India. Architect of non-alignment, Panchsheel. Birth Nov 14 = Children's Day. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel (1875-1950): Iron Man of India. Home Minister, integrated 565 princely states. Bardoli Satyagraha (1928). Birth Oct 31 = Rashtriya Ekta Diwas. Statue of Unity (world's tallest, 182m, Gujarat).
