ir.title: International Relations
ir.content:
India's Foreign Policy — Guiding Principles:
Panchsheel (Five Principles, 1954): Mutual respect for sovereignty, Mutual non-aggression, Mutual non-interference, Equality & mutual benefit, Peaceful coexistence. Co-authored by Nehru & Zhou Enlai. Non-Alignment Movement (NAM, 1961): Founded by Nehru, Tito (Yugoslavia), Nasser (Egypt), Sukarno (Indonesia), Nkrumah (Ghana). HQ not permanent, rotating chair. Gujral Doctrine (1997): Unilateral accommodation of neighbours (non-reciprocal). Look East (1991) → Act East (2014): Focus on ASEAN & East Asia. Neighbourhood First: Priority to SAARC/BIMSTEC neighbours. SAGAR (Security And Growth for All in the Region, 2015): Indian Ocean region policy. Vaccine Maitri (2021): COVID vaccine diplomacy. Connect Central Asia (2012): Central Asia engagement. Think West (2015): West Asia/GCC engagement. Project Mausam (2014): Indian Ocean cultural/economic connectivity.
India & Its Neighbours:
Pakistan: Issues: Kashmir (UN resolutions, Simla Agreement 1972, Lahore Declaration 1999, Agra Summit 2001), Siachen, Sir Creek, terrorism (Mumbai 26/11, Pathankot, Uri, Pulwama), Indus Water Treaty (1960, World Bank mediated). Trade: limited, MFN status revoked 2019. Peace efforts: Agra Summit 2001, Ufa 2015, Lahore visit 2015. China: Issues: Border dispute (McMahon Line, Aksai Chin, Arunachal claim, Doklam 2017, Galwan 2020, Depsang/Demchok), Tibet policy, Pakistan-China nexus, OBOR/BRI opposition. Economic: trade gap in China's favour ($80B+ deficit). Agreements: Panchsheel 1954, Border Peace & Tranquility agreements 1993/1996/2013, Working Mechanism for Consultation & Coordination on India-China Border Affairs (WMCC). Nepal: Special relationship, open border, Sugauli Treaty 1816, Mahakali Treaty (1996) on sharing water from Mahakali. India first responder in 2015 earthquake. Kalapani-Lipulekh border issue. Physical verification: Pancheshwar Multipurpose Project. Bhutan: Indo-Bhutan Friendship Treaty 1949 (revised 2007), joint hydro projects, India guided Bhutan's foreign policy until 2007. Doklam standoff 2017. Bangladesh: Border agreement 1974, Land Boundary Agreement 2015 (enclaves exchanged), Teesta water dispute, Rohingya crisis, trade ~$15B. Issues: illegal migration, border killings. Myanmar: Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Project, India-Myanmar-Thailand trilateral highway. Border fencing issues, free movement regime (FMR) suspended. Sri Lanka: Katchatheevu island dispute, Tamil issue (India's 13th Amendment + Eelam War IV), Colombo port concerns. Economic: India is largest investor, Line of Credit. Maldives: Maritime boundary, Operation Cactus (1988 anti-coup), Maldives-China infrastructure debt concern. Boycott campaigns 2024. Afghanistan: Historical ties (Durand Line issue, Simla 1876), India built Salma Dam, Afghan Parliament, Zaranj-Delaram highway. TAPI pipeline. Chabahar port (Iran) for Afghanistan access.
India & Major Powers:
USA: Strategic partnership (1991 liberalisation → 2005 nuclear deal → 2015 Defence Framework → 2023 iCET). 2+2 Ministerial (Defence + External Affairs). Major defence partner (2016). Quad (India, USA, Japan, Australia). Exercises: Yudh Abhyas (army), Cope India (air), Malabar (naval). Trade ~$190B (2023). Issues: H-1B visas, tariff disputes, CAATSA on S-400 purchase, Russia oil imports. iCET (Initiative on Critical & Emerging Technologies) 2023. Defence: C-17, C-130J, Apache, Chinook, MQ-9B Predator (2024). Russia: Time-tested partner. Defence supplies (60%+ of Indian arsenal). BrahMos joint venture (cruise missile). S-400 Triumf air defence system. Nuclear submarines (Akula-class Nerpa leased). Vostok exercises. India-Russia annual summit (interrupted post-Ukraine 2022). Energy: Sakhalin-I, Russian oil imports surged post-Ukraine war. Issues: Ukraine conflict (India neutral, abstains at UN), Pakistan arms sales (limited). China: (covered above). Japan: Special Strategic & Global Partnership. Shinzo Abe era deepened ties. High-speed rail (Mumbai-Ahmedabad Shinkansen). Infrastructure: India-Japan corridors for NE India, Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor (DMIC). Defence: Malabar exercise advanced, Japan-India 2+2. Nuclear cooperation (Civil nuclear deal). UK: Enhanced Trade Partnership (2030 roadmap), FTA negotiations ongoing. Joint exercises: Ajeya Warrior (army), Konkan (naval). Diaspora: largest in UK. Commonwealth. France: Strategic Partnership (1998). Defence: Rafale jets, Scorpene submarines (Kalvari class), joint exercises (Garuda, Shakti, Varuna). Nuclear cooperation (Jaitapur EPR reactor). Space cooperation. European Union: India-EU Strategic Partnership (2004), FTA negotiations resumed 2022. India-EFTA trade deal (2024, $100B/15yr commitment).
India & Regional Groupings:
UN: Founding member (1945). Permanent member of UNSC aspiration (G4: India, Japan, Germany, Brazil). Reform of UNSC (L.69 group). Financial contributor (peacekeeping, assessed contributions). India largest troop contributor to UN Peacekeeping (200K+ over time). G20: India President 2023 (Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam theme). Key outcomes: African Union as permanent member, digital public infra, LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment). BRICS: Joined BRICS 2009. New Development Bank (NDB, Shanghai) president from India (K.V. Kamath, Dilma Rousseff). 2024 expansion: Iran, Egypt, Ethiopia, UAE, Indonesia added. SCO: Full member 2017 (with Pakistan). Focus: security, terrorism, connectivity, energy. Quad: India+US+Japan+Australia (revitalized 2017, first summit 2021). Focus: Indo-Pacific free & open, maritime security, tech, vaccines. Malabar exercise, Humanitarian Assistance & Disaster Relief (HADR). ASEAN: Summit-level partnership (2002), FTA in goods (2010), services & investment (2015). ASEAN-India Trade Negotiating Committee for review. SAARC: Established 1985, Dhaka. 8 members. South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) 2006. Stalled since 2014 (Pakistan blockage of connectivity). BIMSTEC: Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical & Economic Cooperation (1997). 7 members: India, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Bhutan, Nepal. Replacement venue for SAARC. IORA (Indian Ocean Rim Association): 23 members, 7 dialogue partners. Focus: maritime security, trade, investment. Commonwealth: 56 members. India most populous. Asia-Africa Growth Corridor: India-Japan joint vision (2017). International Solar Alliance (ISA): Launched at COP21 by India & France, HQ Gurugram. 120+ signatories.
India & Global Governance:
WTO: India founding member (1995). Key issues: agriculture subsidies (developed vs developing), fisheries subsidies, moratorium on e-commerce, dispute resolution mechanism reform. India defends developing country interests, food security (public stockholding for food security purposes). IMF & World Bank: Quota reform (India ~2.75% voting share). IMF SDR allocation ($17.86B under 2021 general allocation). World Bank lending ~$3-5B/yr. Climate Governance: UNFCCC (India signed 1993, ratified). Kyoto Protocol. Paris Agreement (ratified 2016). India's NDCs: 500 GW non-fossil by 2030, 50% renewables, 1B ton carbon sink. COP presidency demands: climate finance ($1T), technology transfer. Loss & Damage Fund (advocated at COP27). Nuclear Governance: NSG (Nuclear Suppliers Group) - India waiver 2008 despite non-NPT. India seeks NSG membership (opposed by China). NPT (non-signatory, nuclear weapons state de facto). CTBT (no-signatory, moratorium upheld). FMCT (support). Disarmament: No-first-use policy. Credible minimum deterrent. Against weaponization of outer space. Cyber Governance: Global Cyber Stability framework, India's national cybersecurity strategy. Indian Ocean: Colombo Security Conclave (India, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius, Bangladesh, Seychelles). Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI) 2019.
India's Strategic Neighbourhood & Extended Neighbourhood:
West Asia / Gulf: Energy security (55%+ oil imports from Gulf). Diaspora (8M+ in GCC). Operation Raahat (2015, Yemen evacuation). Operation Sankat Mochan (2016, South Sudan). UAE (CEPA signed 2022). Saudi Arabia (Joint Strategic Partnership Council). Israel (diplomatic relations 1992, upgraded strategic partnership, defence/cyber/agri). Iran (Chabahar port trilateral with Afghanistan). Iraq (oil imports largest supplier). Qatar (LNG supplier, ties upgraded 2024). Central Asia: India-Central Asia Dialogue (first 2022). TAPI pipeline (Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India). Chabahar port (connectivity to Afghanistan & Central Asia). International North South Transport Corridor (INSTC, 2000: Russia-Iran-India). Ashgabat Agreement (2018: transit & transport corridor). Africa: India-Africa Forum Summit (I: 2008, II: 2011, III: 2015). 54 countries. India-Africa trade ~$100B. Defence: military training, joint exercises (Africa-India field training exercise AFINDEX). Lines of Credit ($12B). Development partnership (Pan African e-Network, tele-medicine). Indo-Pacific: India's Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI, 2019) 7 pillars: Maritime Security, Maritime Ecology, Maritime Resources, Capacity Building, Disaster Risk Reduction, Science/Tech, Trade/Connectivity. ASEAN Outlook on Indo-Pacific (AOIP) alignment. Pacific Islands: FIPIC (Forum for India-Pacific Islands Cooperation, 2014). 14 Pacific Island countries. Development cooperation, climate change advocacy.
Key Treaties & Agreements:
• Indus Water Treaty (1960, World Bank) — water sharing of Indus system
• Simla Agreement (1972) — bilateral resolution of Kashmir issues, respect LoC
• Tashkent Declaration (1966) — post Indo-Pak 1965 war resolution
• Lahore Declaration (1999) — peace process, nuclear confidence building
• Agra Summit (2001) — Vajpayee-Musharraf talks, no formal agreement
• Mahakali Treaty (1996) — India-Nepal water resource sharing
• Land Boundary Agreement (2015) — India-Bangladesh enclave exchange (111 enclaves)
• India-US Civil Nuclear Agreement (2005-08) — 123 Agreement, Hyde Act
• India-Japan Civil Nuclear Agreement (2016)
• India-France Civil Nuclear Agreement (2008)
• India-Russia Inter-Governmental Agreements on Kudankulam (1988, 1998)
• Basic Exchange & Cooperation Agreement (BECA, 2020) — India-US geospatial intelligence
• General Security Of Military Information Agreement (GSOMIA, 2002-18 with various)
• Logistics Exchange Memorandum of Agreement (LEMOA, 2016) — India-US military logistics
• Communications Compatibility & Security Agreement (COMCASA, 2018) — India-US secure comms
• ASEAN-India FTA (goods 2010, services & investment 2015)
• India-EFTA Trade & Economic Partnership Act (TEPA, 2024)
• India-UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA, 2022)
• India-Australia Economic Cooperation & Trade Agreement (ECTA, 2022)
• Chahbahar Agreement (2016) — India-Iran-Afghanistan trilateral on Chabahar port
• RCEP (Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership) - India withdrew 2019 (concerns on China trade deficit)
• IPEF (Indo-Pacific Economic Framework, 2022) — India joined on 3 of 4 pillars
• ASEAN-India Maritime Exercise (first 2023)
• India-Japan Act East Forum (2017) — NE India development
• India-Nepal Energy Cooperation Treaty (Electricity cross-border trade)

Indian Diaspora: Largest diaspora in world (32M+, including NRIs + PIOs + OCIs). OCI (Overseas Citizen of India) card since 2005. Pravasi Bharatiya Diwas (Jan 9, since 2003). Major diaspora countries: USA (4.5M+), UAE (3.5M+), Saudi Arabia (2.5M+), UK (1.8M+), Canada (1.6M+), Australia (1M+). Remittances ~$125B (2024, world's largest recipient). Know India Programme (diaspora youth engagement). Pravasi Bharatiya Samman Award (highest honour for diaspora).
India & Global Health: Vaccine Maitri (2021, 60M+ doses to 70+ countries). WHO: India's role in traditional medicine (WHO Global Centre for Traditional Medicine, Jamnagar, 2022). India's pharma exports ~$25B. TRIPS waiver for COVID vaccines (India-South Africa proposal). Global Fund contributions.
India & Tech Diplomacy: Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) model: Aadhaar, UPI, DigiLocker, CoWIN as global templates. India Stack going global (UPI partnerships with 30+ countries). Semiconductor supply chain participation. Quantum computing partnerships. AI governance framework. G20 Digital Public Infrastructure repository (India presidency). India-Brazil-South Africa (IBSA) fund for digital inclusion.
Key IR Terms: Non-proliferation, CTBT, FMCT, NSG, Wassenaar Arrangement, Australia Group, Missile Technology Control Regime (MTCR - India joined 2016), disarmament, deglobalization, friend-shoring, nearshoring, G7, N7 (climate), V20 (vulnerable), MIKTA (Mexico, Indonesia, South Korea, Turkey, Australia), BRICS+, SCO+, I2U2 (India, Israel, UAE, USA), Forum for India-Pacific Islands Cooperation (FIPIC), India-ASEAN, RIC (Russia-India-China trilateral), JAI (Japan-America-India), Quad Plus, CEPA, FTA, PTA, FDI, FPI, ODA, Lines of Credit, SBLC. Currency internationalization (rupee trade). De-dollarization efforts. Chokepoint: Strait of Malacca (25% of world trade, 40% of China trade, 80% of India's oil).

society.title: Indian Society
society.content:
Indian Society — Key Dimensions:
Caste System: Varna (Brahmin/Kshatriya/Vaishya/Shudra) vs Jati (2000+ sub-castes). Origins: Rig Veda (Purusha Sukta). Features: hierarchy, endogamy, hereditary occupation, ritual purity-pollution, civil/religious disabilities. Changes: urbanization, education, land reforms, reservations, Dalit assertion (Bahujan movement, BSP, Mayawati). Caste violence: Khairlanji (2006), Una (2016), Bhima Koregaon (2018). Atrocities against SCs/STs - PoA Act 1989. Mandal Commission (1991, 27% OBC reservation). New economic policy & caste: shrinking of traditional occupations, Dalit entrepreneurs, rise of OBC identity. Census 2011: SC 16.6%, ST 8.6%, OBC ~41% (Mandal, but no caste census to confirm exact). Caste data debate (Socio-Economic Caste Census 2011, not fully released).
Tribal Communities / Scheduled Tribes: 705+ notified STs. 8.6% of population (Census 2011). Largest: Bhil (Guj/MP/Raj), Gond (MP/CG/Mah), Santal (Jharkhand/WB/Odisha). Concentration: NE (Nagaland 86%, Mizoram 95%, Meghalaya 86%), Central India (Chhattisgarh 30%, Jharkhand 26%, Odisha 22%), Andaman & Nicobar (tribes: Sentinelese, Jarawa, Great Andamanese, Onge). Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs): 75 identified (e.g., Sentinelese, Jarawa, Onge, Shompens, Great Andamanese, Birhor, Baiga, Katkari). Constitutional safeguards: 5th Schedule (Central India), 6th Schedule (NE autonomous councils), PESA Act 1996 (panchayat extension to scheduled areas). Issues: land alienation, displacement (mining/dams/forest), Naxalism (Red Corridor - CG/Jharkhand/Odisha/AP/MP), poor health/education, loss of traditional livelihoods. Forest Rights Act 2006 (individual + community forest rights). Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups PVTGs: 75 groups, highest vulnerability. Schemes: PM-JANMAN (2023), Eklavya Model Residential Schools, TRIFED, Van Dhan Yojana.
Women & Gender Issues: Sex ratio (940 females/1000 males, Census 2011). Child sex ratio (918 in 2011, improved to 929 in NFHS-5). Female LFPR (Labour Force Participation) ~32% (2023-24, PLFS). Literacy gap: 82% men vs 65% women (Census 2011). Maternal mortality rate (MMR) ~97/100,000 (2018-20). Key issues: Female feticide (PC&PNDT Act 1994), child marriage (Prohibition of Child Marriage Act 2006, 27% of girls married before 18), dowry (Dowry Prohibition Act 1961, 8,000+ deaths/yr), domestic violence (PWDVA 2005, Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act), workplace harassment (POSH Act 2013, Vishaka guidelines), triple talaq (criminalized 2019), One Stop Crisis Centres, Sakhi/Nirbhaya Fund. Women reservation: 1/3 in Panchayats (73rd/74th Amendment), 106th Amendment (2023, 33% in Lok Sabha & Assemblies - pending implementation). Women-led development: Self-Help Groups (SHGs, 10M+ groups, 130M+ women under Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-NRLM), Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana. Feminist movements & leaders: Savitribai Phule, Pandita Ramabai, Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay, Aruna Asaf Ali, Irom Sharmila, Medha Patkar, Teesta Setalvad, Kiran Bedi, Nirmala Sitharaman, Sushma Swaraj.
Poverty & Inequality: Poverty line: Tendulkar (2011: ₹27 rural, ₹33 urban/day) vs Rangarajan (2014: ₹32 rural, ₹47 urban). Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI): India reduced to 11.28% (NFHS-5 2019-21) from 24.85% (2015-16). NITI Aayog MPI includes health, education, standard of living. Extreme poverty (<$2.15/day) ~2% (IMF 2023). Inequality: Gini coefficient rising (~0.41 consumption, 0.65 income - WID). Top 1% holds ~40%+ of wealth (Oxfam 2024). Rural-urban divide: urban per capita income ~3x rural. Regional inequality: Maharashtra economy > Bangladesh; Bihar per capita ~1/6th Maharashtra. Inclusive growth debate: DBT transfers, MGNREGA, PM-KISAN, food security (NFSA). Global Hunger Index 2024: India rank 105 of 125 (serious).
Urbanization & Migration: Urban population ~36% (2023, Census 2011 was 31%). Projected 40%+ by 2030, 50% by 2047. Megacities: Delhi (32M), Mumbai (21M), Kolkata (15M), Chennai (12M), Bengaluru (12M), Hyderabad (10M). Issues: urban poverty (~25% of urban population lives in slums), housing shortage, traffic congestion, air pollution (Delhi worst globally), water scarcity, solid waste management, open defecation in slums, sewage treatment (~28% urban wastewater treated). Urban governance: 74th Amendment, Urban Local Bodies (municipal corporations, municipal councils, nagar panchayats). Smart Cities Mission (100 cities, 7,800+ projects), AMRUT, PM Awas Yojana (Urban), PM SVANidhi (street vendors). Migration trends: rural-urban seasonal (to construction/domestic work), during COVID massive reverse migration (Parindey, Shramik Special trains). Internal migrants ~40% of population (NSS). Interstate migration: UP-Bihar to Delhi, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Punjab, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu. Remittances within India ~₹2L+ cr/yr. National Migrant Information System (NMIS).
Education & Health: Education: Literacy 74.04% (Census 2011), ~78% (2023). Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER): Primary ~100%, Secondary ~80%, Higher Education ~28% (AISHE 2022). National Education Policy 2020: 5+3+3+4 structure, foundational literacy & numeracy by 2026-27, multiple entry/exit in higher education, Academic Bank of Credit. Key issues: learning poverty (over 50% children cannot read grade-level text - ASER 2023), teacher shortage, high dropout rates at secondary level (boys for economic activity, girls for marriage/care). Female literacy gap: 15%+ vs male. Health: Life expectancy ~70.8 yrs (2023). Infant mortality rate (IMR) ~28/1000 live births. Under-5 mortality ~32. Maternal mortality ~97/100,000. Key issues: malnutrition (35.5% children stunted, 19.3% wasted, 32% underweight - NFHS-5), anaemia (57% women, 31% men), high out-of-pocket expenditure (60%+ health spending), poor public healthcare infrastructure, doctor-patient ratio ~1:800 (better than WHO 1:1000 but uneven), Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY covers 10Cr+ families), PM-ABHIM (Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission). Communicable diseases (TB, malaria, dengue) declining. NCDs rising (diabetes 11% adults, hypertension 25%, cancer).
Communalism & Secularism: Indian secularism: equal respect for all religions (Sarva Dharma Sambhava), no official state religion, freedom of religion (Art 25-28), state neutrality. Communalism: ideology that religious identity is primary political identity. Roots: colonial divide & rule, Partition 1947, communal violence (1984 anti-Sikh, 1992 Babri demolition, 2002 Gujarat, 2013 Muzaffarnagar, 2020 Delhi). NRC & CAA protests 2019-20 (citizenship based on religion vs secularism). Uniform Civil Code (Art 44 DPSP) debate. Religious demography (2011): Hindu 79.8%, Muslim 14.2%, Christian 2.3%, Sikh 1.7%, Buddhist 0.7%, Jain 0.4%, Other 0.7%. Conversion debate: Freedom of Religion Acts in various states (anti-conversion laws). Places of Worship Act 1991 (maintains religious character as of 1947). Waqf Board properties management issue. Minority rights: National Commission for Minorities (1992), 6 religious minorities notified (Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis). No official minority at state level since TMA Pai (2002) ruling changed approach. Multi-faith society: interfaith dialogue, Sufi tradition, Bhakti movement, composite culture (Ganga-Jamuni tehzeeb).
Regionalism & Federal Challenges: Linguistic diversity: 22 scheduled languages, 1,369 mother tongues (Census 2011). Classical languages (6): Tamil, Sanskrit, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Odia. 3-language formula in schools (Hindi, English, regional). Official Language Act 1963: Hindi + English as official languages, no national language. Language riots (anti-Hindi agitation 1960s Tamil Nadu). River water disputes: Cauvery (TN-KA), Krishna (MH-KA-AP), Godavari (MH-KA-AP-TG), Narmada (MP-GJ-MH), Ravi-Beas (PB-HP). Inter-State Council (Art 263). Delimitation Commission for constituency boundaries (frozen until 2026 based on 1971 census). North East insurgency & peace accords (NLFT Tripura, Bodo Assam, NSCN Nagaland - Framework Agreement 2015). Aspirational Districts Programme (112 backward districts). Gorkhaland, Bodoland, Vidarbha, Telangana (achieved 2014), demand for separate states/UTs.
Marginalized Groups & Inclusion: LGBTQ+: Section 377 decriminalized (2018, Navtej Johar), Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act 2019, NALSA judgment (2014) - third gender recognition, same-sex marriage not recognized (SC 2023). Persons with Disabilities: RPwD Act 2016 (21 disabilities, 5% quota in govt jobs, 4% in higher education, 3% in public enterprises), ~2.2% population (Census 2011, likely undercount). Senior Citizens: Maintenance & Welfare of Parents & Senior Citizens Act 2007. 60+/65+ population ~10%. Old Age Pension scheme (NSAP). Beggary & Homeless: State subject, criminalized in some states, SMILE scheme (2021). Children: Child labour (94th Amendment 2010 prohibits <14 age), POCSO Act 2012 (child sexual abuse), Juvenile Justice Act 2015. Street children, child marriage, child trafficking. Migrants & Refugees: Internal labour migrants (COVID highlighted precariousness), UNHCR refugees (Rohingya, Chakma, Sri Lankan Tamil, Afghan, Tibetan), Citizenship Amendment Act 2019 (non-Muslim migrants from Pak/Afghan/Bangladesh).
Important Social Movements & Reformers: Bhakti & Sufi movements (equality, devotion). Brahmo Samaj (Rammohun Roy, 1828). Arya Samaj (Dayanand Saraswati, 1875). Satyashodhak Samaj (Jyotiba Phule, 1873). Ramakrishna Mission (Vivekananda, 1897). Self-Respect Movement (Periyar, 1925). Dalit Buddhist Movement (Ambedkar, 1956). Chipko Movement (1973, environmental). Narmada Bachao Andolan (1985). Right to Information movement (Aruna Roy, MKSS). Anti-corruption movement (Anna Hazare, 2011). Jan Lokpal Bill. #MeToo India (2018). Pinjra Tod (women hostel freedom). Students protests: JNU fee hike (2016), CAA-NRC (2019-20). Farmers' protest (2020-21, 3 farm laws repealed). Shaheen Bagh (CAA protest 2019). Anti-caste movements: Bhima Koregaon, Rohith Vemula suicide (2016). Justice movements: Tawa Matsya Sangh (fisheries), Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan (Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan).
Demographic Dividend & Population: India population ~1.44B (2025, surpassing China). Median age ~29 (vs China 39, Japan 48, US 38). Demographic dividend window: 2005-2055. Youth bulge: 65% under 35. Working age population (15-64) ~68%. Challenges: Skilling gap (only 5% of workforce formally skilled), unemployment ~7-8%, LFPR ~40%, low female participation (~32%). Total Fertility Rate (TFR) ~2.0 (NFHS-5), below replacement (2.1). States: Bihar (3.0) high, WB (1.8) low. Kerala & Goa TFR <1.6. Dependency ratio declining (now ~0.52). NFHS-5 key indicators: anaemia 57%, stunting 35.5%, obesity 24%. Census 2021 delayed (now 2025 likely). Family planning: National Population Policy 2000, family planning voluntary, ASHA workers (10L+), sterilization prevalent. Population Policy 2025 (draft): focus on delayed marriage, spacing, youth health. National Health Mission (NHM) covers family planning.

ethics.title: Ethics & Integrity
ethics.content:
Ethics, Integrity & Aptitude (GS Paper IV):
Ethics — Basic Concepts:
Ethics: Systematic study of moral principles governing human conduct. Derived from Greek "ethos" (character). Morality: practical application of ethics (right/wrong behaviour). Meta-ethics: origin of ethical concepts. Normative ethics: standards of right action (Consequentialism, Deontology, Virtue Ethics). Applied ethics: real-world dilemmas (medical, business, environmental, media). Descriptive ethics: empirical study of moral beliefs.
Foundational Ethical Theories:
• Consequentialism (Teleological): Consequences determine rightness. Utilitarianism (Jeremy Bentham: "greatest good for greatest number", Felicific Calculus; John Stuart Mill: qualitative distinction between higher/low pleasures, rule-utilitarianism). Hedonism: pleasure is ultimate good. Aristotle's Eudaimonia: flourishing/happiness as ultimate goal. Criticism: ignores rights of minorities, difficulty in calculating all consequences.
• Deontology (Kantian Ethics): Duty-based. Immanuel Kant: action is moral if done from duty, not inclination. Categorical Imperative: act according to maxim that becomes universal law; treat humanity as end, never merely as means. Good will is only unconditional good. Distinction between perfect duties (e.g., not lying) and imperfect duties (e.g., charity). Criticism: too rigid, conflicts between duties, ignores consequences.
• Virtue Ethics (Aristotle): Focus on character, not action. Virtues: courage, temperance, justice, wisdom, compassion, honesty, integrity, fortitude. Golden Mean: virtue lies between two extremes (courage between cowardice & recklessness). Phronesis (practical wisdom): knowing right thing at right time. Eudaemonia: human flourishing through virtuous living. Indians: Guru Granth Sahib's five virtues (Sat, Santokh, Daya, Nimrata, Pyaar). Virtues in Indian philosophy: Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya, Brahmacharya, Aparigraha (Jain/Yoga). Contributors: Alisdair MacIntyre (After Virtue). Criticism: not action-guiding, cultural relativity of virtues.
• Ethical Relativism vs Universalism: Relativism: morality varies with culture, no absolute standards. Universalism: certain moral principles hold across all cultures (human rights, dignity). Pluralism: multiple legitimate yet incompatible moral frameworks.
• Rights-based Ethics: John Locke: natural rights (life, liberty, property). W.D. Ross: prima facie duties (fidelity, reparation, gratitude, justice, beneficence, self-improvement, non-maleficence). A.I. Melden: rights protect essential human interests. Criticism: rights may conflict, prioritization needed.
• Justice-based Ethics: Distributive justice (fair allocation of resources). John Rawls (Theory of Justice, 1971): veil of ignorance, original position, two principles (equal basic liberties + fair equality of opportunity + difference principle). Robert Nozick (libertarian, minimal state, entitlement theory). Amartya Sen & Martha Nussbaum: Capabilities Approach (what people are able to do/be).
• Care Ethics: Carol Gilligan: women's moral development emphasizes care, relationships, responsibility. Nel Noddings: care as foundation of ethical action. Contextual, particular, relational vs abstract universal principles.

Integrity & Aptitude for Civil Services:
Integrity: Consistency of actions, values, methods, principles. Components: Honesty (truthfulness, not misleading), Transparency (open about actions/decisions), Accountability (answerable for own actions), Consistency (same principles in all situations). Probity in Governance: absolute integrity, impartiality, non-partisanship, objectivity, dedication to public service, empathy towards vulnerable. Impartiality: no favouritism, treating all citizens equally regardless of caste/religion/class/political affiliation. Objectivity: decisions based on evidence, merit, facts, not personal opinion. Non-partisanship: serving elected government irrespective of personal political views, implementing decisions with same dedication. Dedication to public service: commitment to welfare of citizens, above personal/private gain.
Aptitude: Natural ability/talent for civil service. Required aptitudes: Analytical thinking (problem decomposition), Decision-making (timely, reasoned, participatory), Emotional Intelligence (self-awareness, empathy, managing emotions), Conflict resolution (mediation, negotiation), Communication (clear writing, active listening, public speaking), Leadership (guiding team, vision-setting), Administrative skills (resource utilization, delegation, time management), People skills (dealing with public, understanding vulnerable).
Emotional Intelligence (EI/EQ): Daniel Goleman's 5 components: Self-awareness (knowing own emotions, strengths/limits), Self-regulation (managing impulses, adaptability), Motivation (inner drive, optimism), Empathy (understanding others' feelings, perspective), Social skills (influence, conflict management, collaboration). EI for administrators: better public service, reducing stress, understanding citizen needs, team cohesion, handling pressure. Developing EI: mindfulness, reflection, feedback, active listening, handling criticism.
Civil Service Values:
• Constitutional values: Justice (social/economic/political), Liberty, Equality, Fraternity, Dignity of individual
• Administrative values: Efficiency, Effectiveness, Economy, Equity, Participation
• Democratic values: Rule of law, Transparency, Accountability, Responsiveness
• Personal values: Honesty, Compassion, Courage, Dedication, Humility, Tolerance, Fortitude
• Nolan Committee's 7 Principles of Public Life (UK, 1995): Selflessness, Integrity, Objectivity, Accountability, Openness, Honesty, Leadership
• 2nd ARC recommendations: Code of Ethics for civil servants, integrity pact, whistleblower protection, ethical audit

Ethical Dilemmas in Public Administration:
Resource allocation (limited funds between competing needs). Rule vs discretion (strictly follow rules vs bend for humanitarian needs). Impartiality vs relationship (treating relative/friend equally). Transparency vs confidentiality (RTI vs national security). Private vs public interest (conflict of interest, nepotism). Neutrality vs conscience (implementing policy you disagree with). Rule of law vs justice (letter of law vs equitable outcome). Efficiency vs equity (fast decisions vs fair inclusion). Transparency vs privacy (disclosing confidential info for public good). Resolution framework: 1) Identify ethical dimensions, 2) Identify stakeholders, 3) Consider alternative actions, 4) Apply ethical theories (consequences, duties, virtues), 5) Check consistency with values, 6) Make decision, 7) Justify transparently. Case study approach: UPSC typically presents administrative dilemma requiring: stakeholder analysis, ethical dimension identification, alternative evaluation, decision with justification, long-term systemic solution.
Corruption & Anti-Corruption Mechanisms:
Types of corruption: Petty (bribe for service), Grand (high-level policy capture), Political (electoral, party funding), Bureaucratic (rent-seeking, speed money). Causes: complexity of rules, monopoly power, discretion without accountability, low salaries, weak enforcement. Prevention: Transparency (RTI Act 2005, proactive disclosure), E-governance (less human interface, DBT, online procurement), Simplification (single window, faceless assessment), Whistleblower protection (Whistleblowers Protection Act 2014, though implementation weak), Citizen Charters (Service guarantee, right to service acts in 22 states), Social audit (MGNREGA mandatory). Institutions: CVC (Central Vigilance Commission, 1964), CBI (Central Bureau of Investigation, 1963), Lokpal & Lokayuktas Act 2013 (anti-corruption ombudsman, holds PM/Cabinet/judges accountable). Preventive Vigilance: Chief Technical Examiner, Chief Engineer vigilance cells, surprise visits, transparent tendering, e-procurement (Govt e-Marketplace-GEM). Integrity pact (transparency & fairness). Asset declarations of public servants (mandatory for IAS/IPS/IFS, annual). International: UN Convention against Corruption (UNCAC 2003, India ratified 2011). FATF (India member, mutual evaluation done). OECD Anti-Bribery Convention (India not member).
Important Laws & Codes for Civil Servants:
• All India Services (Conduct) Rules 1968 — general conduct, gifts, investments, political neutrality
• All India Services (Discipline & Appeal) Rules 1969 — disciplinary proceedings, penalties
• Prevention of Corruption Act 1988 (amended 2018) — criminalizes bribery, creates offense for bribe-giver too
• Public Interest Disclosure & Protection of Informers (Whistleblowers) Act 2014
• Right to Information Act 2005 — transparency, citizens right to know
• Official Secrets Act 1923 — unauthorized disclosure of official information criminalized
• Civil Services Rules (CCS) — code of conduct
• 2nd Administrative Reforms Commission (ARC) Reports — recommendations on ethics, governance
• National Commission to Review Working of Constitution (NCRWC, Venkatachaliah Commission)
• Citizens Charter initiative (1997, SC Gupta committee)
• Sevottam (excellence in public service delivery)
• National e-Governance Plan (NeGP), Mission Mode Projects
• Model Code of Conduct (Election Commission, for political parties)

Ethical Thinkers & Philosophers:
Western: Socrates (question everything, unexamined life not worth living), Plato (justice as harmony, ideal state, philosopher-king), Aristotle (virtue ethics, golden mean, polis), Kant (deontology, categorical imperative), Bentham (utilitarianism, pleasure-pain calculation), Mill (rule-utilitarianism, liberty, harm principle), Rawls (justice as fairness, difference principle), Nozick (minimal state, entitlement), Sen (capabilities, development as freedom), Singer (effective altruism, animal liberation). Indian: Buddha (middle path, compassion, non-harm, mindfulness), Mahavira (ahimsa paramo dharma, anekantavada, aparigraha), Gandhi (satyagraha, non-violence, trusteeship, swadeshi, simple living, sarvodaya), Vivekananda (universal brotherhood, practical Vedanta, service to man = service to God), Tagore (humanism, universalism, nationalism critique), Ambedkar (social justice, constitutional morality, annihilation of caste), Sri Aurobindo (integral yoga, evolution of consciousness), Jiddu Krishnamurti (radical freedom, self-knowledge, no authority). Comparative: duty (Kant) vs consequences (Bentham) — applied to public administration. Indian ethos: dharma (righteous duty), karma (action without attachment to results - Gita), lokasangraha (welfare of all), vasudhaiva kutumbakam (world as family), sarvodaya (uplift of all, Gandhi), antodaya (uplift of last person).
